children.translated_text: <s>Abhinanda</s>: <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>

children.text: śriyaṃ diśantu vaḥ śaurer dvaye tulyaśramāḥ kramāḥ /
children.translated_text: May the strides of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), equal in effort yet twofold, bestow prosperity upon you —

children.text: ye cādau goṣpadaṃ paścāt trailokyaṃ krāmyataś ca ye //
children.translated_text: Those which at first [covered] a cow's hoof-print, and later [those] which traversed the three worlds.
The speeches of <s>Jayanta</s>, teacher of the world, father's [son], are eloquent, well-adorned,
Sweet in their clarity, and lovely — they are triumphant!
The virtuous are lamps for illuminating the qualities [of others]; there is nothing supremely brilliant [about them] —

children.text: yāvan malinam apy eṣāṃ karma dṛṣṭeḥ prasādhanam //
children.translated_text: Even the tarnished deeds of these [others] serve as an ornament for their vision.

children.text: guṇaḥ kṛśo 'pi prathate pṛthur apy apacīyate /
children.translated_text: A virtue, even if small, spreads wide; [a virtue], even if great, diminishes,

children.text: prāpya sādhukhalau candraḥ pakṣāv iva sitāsitau //
children.translated_text: When it encounters the good and the wicked — like the moon [encountering] its bright and dark fortnights.
There was a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Gauḍa</s> [country], of the <s>Bhāradvāja</s> lineage, named <s>Śakti</s>,
Who, having arrived at <s>Dārvābhisāra</s>, took a wife.
He had a son named <s>Mitra</s>, a treasury of splendor,
Whose rise was honored by people awakened to the cessation of faults.
He obtained a son named <s>Śaktisvāmin</s>, learned in scripture,
Who became a minister to the king of the <s>Karkoṭa</s> dynasty, <s>Muktāpīḍa</s>.
A son named <s>Kalyāṇasvāmin</s> was born to him, like <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,
Whose sins of worldly existence were dispelled by the prosperity of pure <s>yoga</s>.
From that one of unfathomable heart, a son was born

children.text: ajāyata sutaḥ kāntaś candro dugdhodadher iva //
children.translated_text: Who was an ornament of Lord <s>Parameśvara</s>, lovely like the moon [born] from the ocean of milk.
He begot a son named <s>Jayanta</s>, who brought joy to all people,
Whose <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning) bore the fruits of poetic skill and eloquence.

children.text: vṛttikāra iti vyaktaṃ dvitīyaṃ nāma bibhrataḥ /
children.translated_text: He also bore the second name '<s>Vṛttikāra</s>' (commentator), manifestly,
Being learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, expounding the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s>.
From that wise <s>Jayanta</s>, who knew the true essence of good literature,

children.text: sūnuḥ samudabhūt tasmād abhinanda iti śrutaḥ //
children.translated_text: A son arose, known as <s>Abhinanda</s>.
[A couplet:]
For those whose minds are weary from the effort of composing an extensive poem,
By him was extracted merely the story from the ocean of <s>Kādambarī</s>.
There was a city named <s>Vidiśā</s>, an ornament of the earth,
Whose splendor rivaled the city of <s>Indra</s>, situated on the bank of the <s>Vetravatī</s> river.
Which, like heaven, was the abode of those of meritorious deeds and brilliant prowess,
And which shone with clusters of lights from jeweled mansions, resplendent like rainbows.
*[A couplet:]*
In that [city], there was a glorious king named <s>Śūdraka</s>, like <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: ākhaṇḍala iva śrīmān rājā śūdraka ity abhūt //
children.translated_text: Who had conquered the circle of enemies by the effort of his own arms.

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ lokapālānāṃ rūpaṃ bibhrad api prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Though bearing the form of the eight <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), he constantly delighted his subjects,

children.text: śaśvad ānandayaṃs tābhiś candramā ity avedi yaḥ //
children.translated_text: And was therefore known as the moon [itself].
*[A couplet:]*
Having conquered the earth girdled by four oceans,
He entrusted its burdens to his ministers and dwelt therein at ease.
By him, whose people were not distressed, through pastimes that did not conflict with <s>artha</s> (wealth) and <s>dharma</s> (duty),
The days were passed in the bloom of youth.
And his mind, which had seen the limits of pleasures unattainable by others,
Even in youth, was turned away from the sport of love.
There was not even a single woman whom the flower-arrowed god (<s>Kāma</s>), even with great effort,

children.text: hartuṃ śaśāka yā tasya hṛdayaṃ cakṣur eva vā //
children.translated_text: Was able to use to steal either his heart or even his gaze.
Then once, when he was standing in the outer courtyard,
The door-keeper woman, having approached, bowing with affection, announced —
"A certain <s>Caṇḍāla</s> maiden, having brought a parrot of wonderful behavior as an offering,
Has come seeking an audience."

children.text: śrutvā kṣaṇaṃ parāmṛśya mukham ālokya mantriṇām /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, reflecting for a moment, and looking at the faces of his ministers,

children.text: samādideśa tāṃ rājā ko doṣaḥ praviśatv iti //
children.translated_text: The king instructed her: "What fault is there? Let her enter."
Then, avoiding contact with people through her own characteristic marks,
The <s>Mātaṅga</s> maiden, having been permitted, entered the royal courtyard.
And along with her, carrying a golden cage with a parrot in hand,
An old <s>Caṇḍāla</s> man of harmless appearance entered.

children.text: praviśantīṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyām adbhutadarśanām /
children.translated_text: Seeing that maiden of wondrous appearance entering,

children.text: paraṃ vyasmayata kṣmāpaḥ kṣaṇaṃ caivam acintayat //
children.translated_text: The king was greatly astonished and for a moment thought thus —

children.text: idaṃ rūpam iyaṃ kāntir ime lāvaṇyaśīkarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "This beauty, this radiance, these drops of charm

children.text: martyatām api na prāhurmātaṅgatve tu kā kathā //
children.translated_text: Do not even betoken mortality — and what to say of <s>Mātaṅga</s> [birth]!"

children.text: tat satyam eva paśyāmi nūnaṃ mātaṅgamāyayā /
children.translated_text: "Truly I perceive that, concealed by the <s>māyā</s> (magic) of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>,
This is surely some deity who has come to the mortal world."
While he was thinking such thoughts, she, like a bold woman,
Bowed to the king, gazing without confusion.
Then the old man, with knees placed on the ground, his neck bowed,
With both hands firmly holding the cage, spoke —
"This parrot named <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> is a most wondrous jewel,
And the lord is the repository of jewels, like a second ocean of milk."
"With this regard, this [parrot] has been brought by our master's daughter as an offering.
May your grace be shown — let the bird be accepted."

children.text: ity uktvā so 'grato rājñaḥ pañjaraṃ maṇikuṭṭime /
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken, he placed the cage before the king on the jeweled floor,
Bowed to him, and respectfully withdrew.
The perceptive door-keeper opened the door of the cage,

children.text: akarot pañjaraṃ tasmān niryayau ca vihaṅgamaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the bird emerged from it.

children.text: utkṣipya dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ jayaśabdam udīrya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Raising his right foot, uttering the word 'Victory!',
He pronounced blessings in proper <s>Vedic</s> mantras and then recited this noble verse —
"The breast-pair of your enemy's wives wanders about, bathed in tears, near the fire of heart's grief,

children.text: carati vimuktāhāraṃ vratam iva bhavato ripustrīṇām //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned food — like a vow of your [glory]."
Having heard that, the king, with eyes wide open in astonishment,
Addressed his chief minister named <s>Kumārapāla</s> —

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ bhavadbhir āścaryam īdṛśaṃ śrutam eva vā /
children.translated_text: "Have you ever seen or heard of such a marvel?
What is this extraordinary [accomplishment] in an animal birth that is rare even among humans?"
"The refinement of Vedic study, the association with <s>Mātaṅga</s> people,
And this maiden among the <s>Mātaṅgas</s> — wonder upon wonder!"
The minister replied: "O lord, extraordinary [attainments] caused by previous-life impressions

children.text: bhavanty atiśayāḥ prāyaḥ prāṇināṃ ko 'tra vismayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Generally occur in living beings — what wonder is there in this?"
"These are the very signs regarding the inference of the other world
That are established by logicians in the refutation of the <s>Lokāyatas</s> (materialists)."
"The creation of the Creator is wondrous, the imprint of <s>karma</s> is wondrous,
Its ripening is wondrous, and the revolution of time is wondrous."
And so on — but the cause of the interruption of the story related to the parrot
Was the deep-toned sound of the midday drum that arose.
"Let comfortable lodgings and the like be arranged outside for her,
And let this king of birds be brought inside."

children.text: ity ādiśya pratīhārīṃ sabhām aujjhan mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the door-keeper, the king left the assembly hall
And dismissed the circle of nobles who had come to render service.
Then, having performed some exercise, bathed, worshipped the deities,
Made offerings to the sacred fire, heard the blessings of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and eaten, he went to the bed-chamber.

children.text: tatra paryaṅkam āruhya dhyātvaiva kim api kṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: There, having ascended the couch and meditated for a moment on something,
He had the parrot, which was resting in the inner apartments, brought again.
First asking the [parrot], who had been brought by a chamberlain, about his comfort in sitting,
He then asked, seized with curiosity, about his story.

children.text: vaiśampāyana ko nu tvaṃ kva jātaḥ kvoṣitaś ciram /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, who are you? Where were you born? Where did you dwell for a long time?
From where comes this skill of yours in the arts, sciences, and the like?"

children.text: manye jātismaraḥ ko 'pi bhavān bhūmim imāṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: "I think you are some <s>jātismara</s> (one who remembers previous births) who has come to this earth,

children.text: na hy asty atiśayaprāptir iyatī pakṣijātiṣu //
children.translated_text: For such extraordinary attainment does not exist in the species of birds."

children.text: kena vā bhavato nāma kṛtaṃ viprajanocitam /
children.translated_text: "By whom was this name, befitting a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, given to you?
From where do such names come in the dwellings of the lowest castes?"

children.text: kathaṃ caṇḍālasamparka iha vā katham āgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "How is it that there is contact with <s>Caṇḍālas</s>? And how did you come here?

children.text: iti kārtsnyena vṛttāntam ātmano vaktum arhasi //
children.translated_text: Please relate your story in its entirety."
Thus questioned by the king with great respect,
The parrot, having reflected for a moment with his intellect, began to speak.
"O lord, the <s>Vindhya</s> forest, which touches the shores of both the eastern and western oceans,
Has first come within the range of your hearing."
"In one part of which, among trees broken by the itching cheeks of elephants,
<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, together with <s>Sītā</s>, dwelt in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest."
*[A couplet:]*
"Where there was the hermitage of the sage <s>Agastya</s>, revered by the tranquil ones,
Its trees nourished by the water drawn by the hands of <s>Lopāmudrā</s>."
"Near it there is a lake called <s>Pampā</s>, with sacred waters,
Its lotuses plucked by the hands of <s>Sītā</s> to serve as ear-ornaments."
"On its western bank there is an ancient <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) tree,
Whose height and girth fill the space between sky and horizon."
"In that inaccessible [tree], having built their nests, free from fear,
Thousands of birds dwell without interruption."

children.text: divā tāny abhinirvartya prāṇayātrām itas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: "By day, they go forth here and there accomplishing their sustenance,
Then returning there, they sleep comfortably in their nests at night."
"Right there, having established their dwelling, were my parents.

children.text: jāto 'ham ekas tanayas tayor vayasi paścime //
children.translated_text: I was born as their only son, in their late years."
"Unable to bear the intense pain of childbirth,

children.text: tayaiva pañcatāṃ nītā jananī me durātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: My mother was brought to death by it — wretched that I am."
"Though burned by separation from his wife, my father, tormented by desire for his son,
Cast aside his grief and took up the effort of nourishing my life."

children.text: na śaśāka kvacid gantum ātmanaḥ prāṇavṛttaye /
children.translated_text: "He was unable to go anywhere for the sustenance of his own life;

children.text: māṃ vakṣasi nidhāyāsta nīḍa eva divāniśam //
children.translated_text: Placing me on his breast, he remained in the nest day and night."
"With the remnants left over from feeding me, [food] brought by other birds
Such as abandoned fruits and the like, he sustained his own life."
"As time passed, when my wings had slightly emerged
And I, though still on my father's breast, was eager to fly —"
"Suddenly, in that forest, the sound of a tumult was heard,
From the frightened herds of deer and flocks of birds — like the drum of <s>Yama</s> (death)."
[A couplet:]
"Then, raising my head a little from my father's breast,
I, impelled by curiosity, cast my eyes in all directions."
"Then I saw, surrounded by countless <s>Kirātas</s> (tribesmen),
The <s>Śabara</s> (tribal) chieftain approaching, intoxicated with the thrill of the hunt."

children.text: tato mṛtam ivātmānam utkhātam iva śālmalim /
children.translated_text: "Then, with fear, I thought of myself as dead,
The <s>śālmali</s> tree as uprooted, and the forest as overturned."
"Within a moment, that forest was filled by those hunters,
Smeared with the flowing blood from the limbs of thousands of slain creatures."
"That chieftain, sword in hand, fatigued from the hunt,
Then sat down on the green grass on the shore of Lake <s>Pampā</s>."
"Having rested for a moment, drunk some water, and eaten young lotus stalks,

children.text: pulindaiḥ saha senānīḥ sa jagāma yathāgatam //
children.translated_text: The chieftain went back with the <s>Pulindas</s> (tribesmen) the way he had come."

children.text: eko jaratpulindas tu pāpas tatra vyalambata /
children.translated_text: "But one aged, wicked <s>Pulinda</s> lingered there,
Tall, of terrifying appearance, like a servant of Death."
"Having failed to obtain any flesh, having endured fruitless toil,

children.text: yamadūtīm iva dṛśaṃ sa dadau tatra śālmalau //
children.translated_text: He cast his gaze — like the messenger of <s>Yama</s> — upon that <s>śālmali</s> tree."

children.text: sa durārohatāṃ tasya jānann api mahātaroḥ /
children.translated_text: "Though knowing the great tree to be difficult to climb,
And though lacking determination, he made an effort to ascend."
"Then I, my mind overturned by boundless terror,
Entered my father's lap, my body covered by his wings."

children.text: sa tu pāpas tam āruhya taruṃ nīḍanivāsinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "But that wicked one, having climbed the tree,

children.text: hatvā hatvā yathāśakti śukān bhūmāv apātayat //
children.translated_text: Killed the parrots dwelling in their nests one by one as best he could and threw them to the ground."
"Gradually, that evil-doer also broke the neck

children.text: babhañja taṃ ca cikṣepa kṣitau vigatajīvitam //
children.translated_text: Of my father and hurled him to the ground, devoid of life."

children.text: tadā mama na tacchoko nānyat kiñcic ca cetasi /
children.translated_text: "At that time, neither grief for my father nor anything else was in my mind;
I was overwhelmed solely by innate fear."
"Then, emerging trembling from my father's lap,
I quickly entered among the withered leaves of the tree."
"That wicked one, having descended from the <s>śālmali</s> tree,

children.text: śukān gatāsūn ādāya vyādhān anusarann agāt //
children.translated_text: Took the dead parrots at its base and went off following the hunters."
"But I, by the decree of fate, was not noticed at that time by that evildoer,
Because of my resemblance in color to the withered leaves."
"Then, when he of cruel deeds had gone far away,
Thirst began to torment me, who had now regained hope for life."
"Unable to fly, on foot only, somehow,
I wished, though thirsty, to reach the shore of Lake <s>Pampā</s>."

children.text: tathāpy atinirutsāhaḥ patan muhur itas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Yet, being utterly without vigor, falling repeatedly here and there,

children.text: tam eva pāpakarmāṇaṃ śaṅkamānaḥ pade pade //
children.translated_text: Suspecting that evil-doer at every step —"

children.text: ciraṃ hā tāta tāteti śocan kaṇṭhāntavartibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Grieving for a long time, crying 'Alas, father, father!', with life-breaths
lingering at the edge of my throat, I remained, utterly wretched.
*couplet*
Not far from that lake was the hermitage of the sage
<s>Jābāli</s>, a treasury of austerities, who had shaken off the net of afflictions.

children.text: tatas tasmin sutas tasya sarasi snātum āgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, his son, having come to bathe in that lake,
named <s>Hārīta</s>, saw me there in that condition.
'Alas! A parrot chick, cast down by some sinful creature,
languishes from its nest!' — saying this, he took me in his hand out of compassion.
He gave me drops of milk, reviving me again and again with breaths of air,

children.text: kṛtāhnikaś ca kāruṇyād anayat pitur āśramam //
children.translated_text: and having completed his daily rites, out of pity, he brought me to his father's hermitage.
As I, now revived, beheld the father of <s>Hārīta</s> with my eyes,

children.text: padaṃ sthiram iva nyastaṃ hṛdi me jīvitāśayā //
children.translated_text: it was as if a firm foothold had been placed in my heart by the hope of life.
'This bird-chick, fallen from its nest, has been brought by me' —
thus bowing to his father, he showed me, held in his hand.

children.text: atha jābālim adrākṣaṃ sākṣād iva pitāmaham /
children.translated_text: Then I beheld <s>Jābāli</s>, as if he were my grandfather himself,
surrounded by great-souled ascetics full of compassion.
His head white with old age, with radiance spreading outward,
the contours of his bodily limbs barely discernible.

children.text: sa tu māṃ kṣaṇam udvīkṣya smayamāna ivāvadat /
children.translated_text: He, gazing at me for a moment, spoke as if smiling:

children.text: idaṃ hi bhujyate 'nena phalaṃ svasyaiva karmaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, this one is experiencing the fruit of his own actions.'
For that blessed one, seer of the three times, with his divine eye,
beholds the entire universe as if it were a <s>badara</s> (jujube) or <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) in his hand.

children.text: vacas tad ākarṇya kutūhalākulāḥ sametya sarve munayas ta mabruvan /
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech, the sages, agitated with curiosity, gathered together and said to him:

children.text: babhūva ko 'yaṃ bhagavan bhavāntare kim asya vā duścaritaṃ tad ucyatām //
children.translated_text: 'Who was this one in a previous birth, O blessed one? Or what was his misdeed? Let it be told.'

children.text: abhyarthito munibhir ity uparudhyamānas tān abravīt kuruta tāvadahaḥkriyāḥ svāḥ /
children.translated_text: Entreated thus by the sages, detained by them, he said: 'First complete your daily rites;

children.text: sāṃdhyaṃ vidhāya vidhim askhalitāvadhānam ākarṇayiṣyatha kathāṃ pṛthum etadīyām //
children.translated_text: having performed the twilight rituals, with undivided attention, you shall hear his lengthy story.'

children.text: uktās tathā bhagavatā munayo nijena karmakrameṇa divasaṃ gamayāṃbabhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: The sages, thus addressed by the blessed one, spent the day with their own routine of rites;

children.text: hārītahastavihitaiś ca manovinodais tais tair ānīyata mayāpi dināvaśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: and by me too, the remainder of the day was passed with various diversions provided by <s>Hārīta</s>'s hand.

Thus ends the first canto of the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the teacher, the venerable <s>Jayanta</s>, foremost among the assembly of the most distinguished scholars.
Second Canto
Then the sages, having completed their rites ending with the twilight meditation,
gathered together, eager to listen, and sat in their respective places.
I too, eager to hear the full account of my own history,

children.text: saṃhṛtya cāpalaṃ sarvam āsaṃ sthiramanās tadā //
children.translated_text: restraining all my restlessness, sat with a steady mind at that time.
Then, with rays white as the waves of the milk-ocean,
adorned with nectar, the moon rose, as if sprinkling the hermitage grounds with its beams.
The blessed <s>Jābāli</s>, comfortably seated on his own seat,
assuming a cross-legged posture arranged on bark-cloth, began to speak:
'All of you, O ascetics, give your attention! Hear
this story, occasioned by the introduction of this one's previous history.'
'In the land of the <s>Avantis</s>, as if the birthplace of the splendor of worldly existence,
there is a city named <s>Ujjayinī</s>, a treasure-house of the wealth of virtues.
Even those whose beloved dwellings are <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Alakā</s>, and <s>Amarāvatī</s>,

children.text: te 'pi yām abhipaśyantaḥ sukhaṃ tāsu na śerate //
children.translated_text: upon beholding her, do not sleep contentedly in those [cities].
What more — where, abandoning the delight of dwelling on <s>Kailāsa</s>,
<s>Rudra</s> himself resides under the name <s>Mahākāla</s>.'
*tilaka verse*
'In that [city], comparable to <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, <s>Bhagīratha</s>, and <s>Pṛthu</s>,
there was a glorious king named <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>.
Where all virtues, scattered here and there by their mutual opposition,

children.text: visrabdham āsyate yatra sambhūya sakalair guṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: gather together and reside in confidence.
*couplet*
Surpassing in intellectual powers both <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the preceptor of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s lineage, while laughing [at their rivalry],
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Śukanāsa</s> was his minister.
That king, having conquered this earth like <s>Trivikrama</s>'s step,
deposited its burden upon that minister, who was capable of bearing it.

children.text: tathā ca pālayāmāsa sa mantrī sakalāḥ prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: And that minister governed all the subjects in such a manner

children.text: yathā trividham apy etā na duḥkhaṃ kiñcid aspṛśan //
children.translated_text: that they were not touched by any suffering of the three kinds.
And as the people increasingly became devoted to him as to a father,
so did the king increasingly consider himself fulfilled.
Having effortlessly deposited the task of governing the world upon his own arm,
he handed over the administration to the minister, considering governance an obstruction to his enjoyment.
And considering himself fulfilled, without concern for remaining duties,
with his affections directed toward pleasures, he indulged as he pleased.
For the wealth of enjoyments is indeed an adornment for a king who has accomplished his duties;
but for one whose ambition to conquer remains unfulfilled, those same become a mockery.
He, young, of sweet appearance, a festival for the eyes of young women,
skilled in the arts, amorous, enjoyed the wealth of pleasures.

children.text: na te bhogā na tāḥ krīḍā na tā goṣṭhyo na te rasāḥ /
children.translated_text: There were no pleasures, no diversions, no assemblies, no aesthetic delights,

children.text: na te vilāsā yeṣv asya pāragaṃ nābhavan manaḥ //
children.translated_text: no amorous sports in which his mind did not reach the farthest shore.
Though that king was versed in the realm of complete enjoyment of all happiness,
one happiness alone he did not know — that born of beholding offspring.

children.text: yathā yathāsya kālena vyatīyāya navaṃ vayaḥ /
children.translated_text: As his fresh youth passed with time,

children.text: nirapatyatayā śoko vardhate sma tathā tathā //
children.translated_text: so did his grief grow on account of being childless.
And the chief queen among his entire <s>antaḥpura</s> (inner palace),
named <s>Vilāsavatī</s>, was as dear to him as his own life-breath.
That royal consort, wishing to worship <s>Gaurī</s> one day,
went to an outlying temple with her husband's permission.
While a <s>Purāṇa</s> was being recited, she happened to hear the passage:

children.text: aputrasya kuto lokā iti śuśrāva tatra sā //
children.translated_text: 'Where are the heavenly worlds for one without a son?'
That verse entered her ear-passage like a red-hot needle,

children.text: viveśa dadatī tasyāḥ parāṃ kām api vedanām //
children.translated_text: giving her some indescribable pain.
Then, having returned and entered her own palace,
with her face covered by her garment, she sat on the ground and wept.

children.text: sakhībhiḥ prārthyamānāpi na svām abhajata sthitim /
children.translated_text: Even when entreated by her companions, she did not recover her composure;

children.text: nodasthāt kartum āhāraṃ virarāma na rodanāt //
children.translated_text: she did not rise to take food and did not cease weeping.
Then the king, learning from the attendants of her distress and affliction,
entered the inner chambers and spoke to her gently, trying to console her:

children.text: priye kim idam ārabdhaṃ rudyate kim akāraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Dear one, what has been begun? Why do you weep without cause?

children.text: na tvayā matkṛte manyur anubhūtaḥ kadācana //
children.translated_text: Never has anger been experienced by you on my account.
Moreover, who else — one who looks to my face, whose life depends on me —

children.text: kas tavotpādayen manyuṃ yasmai kupyasi sundari //
children.translated_text: could cause you anger? At whom are you angry, O beautiful one?'

children.text: iti prasādyamānā sā yadā novāca kiñcana /
children.translated_text: When she, though being consoled, would say nothing at all,
then the king was informed of the circumstances by her friend.
By that turn of events, he too became overcome with grief
and wept, with the tear-stained face of his beloved pressed to his chest.

children.text: ciraṃ ruditvā niḥśabdaṃ svayam unmṛjya locane /
children.translated_text: Having wept silently for a long time, wiping his own eyes,
the king spoke falteringly, consoling his queen:

children.text: mamāpi nanv iyaṃ devi cirāt prabhṛti duḥsahā /
children.translated_text: 'My queen, indeed this intolerable anxiety
has been tormenting my heart too for a long time, like an incurable disease.

children.text: viphalaṃ bata me rājyaṃ viphalā mama sampadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fruitless indeed is my kingdom, fruitless are my riches,

children.text: viphalā mama sambhogā viphalaṃ mama jīvitam //
children.translated_text: fruitless are my pleasures, fruitless is my very life.
Whence would such abundance of fortune come to us, the ill-fated,
that we might behold your lap adorned by a little child?

children.text: vāñchan krīḍanakaṃ kiñcit kadā me pāpakarmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: When will a son of mine, a sinner, desiring some toy,

children.text: ākṛṣyati sutaḥ kūrcaṃ kim apy avyaktam ālapan //
children.translated_text: pull at my beard, babbling something indistinctly?'
While he was lamenting thus, his eyes flooded with tears,
<s>Śukanāsa</s>, having heard this news, came hastily.
He too had been made childless, as if by the same hostile fate, just like the king;

children.text: tasyāpy anena śokena gṛhe roditi gehinī //
children.translated_text: and on account of this sorrow, his wife too wept at home.

children.text: sa tu svāmigataṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkham ity avadhārayan /
children.translated_text: But he, considering the suffering of his master as his own suffering,
intent on the means to remove that sorrow, spoke firmly:
'Where is the lord's naturally steadfast disposition, and where is this agitation of mind?
Grief finds no room in the hearts of those such as you.

children.text: yadi hi strīsvabhāvena devī viklavatāṃ gatā /
children.translated_text: If indeed the queen has become agitated due to feminine nature,

children.text: tat kiṃ pralambakūrcasya yuktaṃ devasya roditum //
children.translated_text: is it then fitting for the lord, who wears a long beard, to weep?
What kind of procedure for attaining benefit and averting harm is this,
that one sighs for long with hand placed on the cheek?
If your sorrow is truly on account of childlessness,
let your mind be applied to <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) — a festival of <s>dharma</s> will be attained.
Let wealth be given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, let all deities be worshipped,
let public rest-houses and gardens be established, let reservoirs be excavated.

children.text: nāsti nāma jagaty asmin puruṣārthaḥ sa kaścana /
children.translated_text: There is no human goal whatsoever in this world
that is not attained by steadfast ones like you who are devoted to <s>dharma</s>.'
Hearing these and other words of <s>Śukanāsa</s>, the royal couple, their fever gone,

children.text: utthāya svasthavat sarvā dampatī cakratuḥ kriyāḥ //
children.translated_text: rose and performed all their duties as if restored to health.
From then on, the two performed extraordinary gifts, sacrifices, fire-offerings, and austerities,

children.text: citrāṇy akurutāṃ sarvā vyasmayanta tataḥ prajāḥ //
children.translated_text: at which all the people marveled.
Once, the king saw in a dream the moon
entering the face of <s>Vilāsavatī</s>, whole and undiminished.
Likewise, <s>Manoramā</s>, the wife of <s>Śukanāsa</s>,
was also seen by him in a dream, bearing the mark of a white lotus.
The next day, at sunrise, with auspicious ceremonies,
the king related that dream to <s>Śukanāsa</s>.

children.text: sānandaṃ so 'bhyadhād enaṃ sampannās te manorathāḥ /
children.translated_text: With joy, he told him: 'Your desires have been fulfilled;
soon the queen will give birth to a son beautiful as the full moon.'

children.text: dineṣv atha vyatīteṣu keṣucid garbham agrahīt /
children.translated_text: Then, after some days had passed, the queen conceived;

children.text: mahiṣī tatsakhībhyaś ca tam ajñāsīn nareśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: and the king learned of it from her companions.

children.text: tābhyaḥ prādāt sa vāsāṃsi citrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: He gave them splendid garments and ornaments,
and as the signs of pregnancy gradually became manifest, he rejoiced exceedingly.
And he said to <s>Śukanāsa</s>, his eyes wide open with delight,
eagerly anticipating the day of delivery, as a <s>cātaka</s> bird [awaits] rain clouds.

children.text: sampūrṇe daśame māsi devī sutam asūta sā /
children.translated_text: When the tenth month was completed, the queen gave birth to a son,

children.text: harṣeṇa ca jagat sarvaṃ parivṛttam ivābhavat //
children.translated_text: and the entire world seemed to be transformed with joy.
The king, seeing the vessel of great celebration-joy brought forth,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokeṣu māti sma na trivikramavat triṣu //
children.translated_text: gloried — not like <s>Trivikrama</s> in the three worlds [but in his own way].

children.text: śukanāsas tu rājānaṃ kaṇṭhe jagrāha nirbharam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śukanāsa</s> embraced the king tightly around the neck;

children.text: autsukyāt sūtikāvāsaṃ tāv ubhāv api jagmatuḥ //
children.translated_text: and the two of them, in their eagerness, went to the birthing chamber.
Then they beheld the infant prince with all his limbs clearly formed,
like a fresh orb of the moon risen, moist with the glow of rising.
<s>Śukanāsa</s>, carefully examining each limb of the child,
taking the king by the hand, spoke with a voice full of joy:

children.text: ayaṃ śaṅkha idaṃ cakram iyam ūrṇedam ambujam /
children.translated_text: 'This is the conch, this the discus, this the spiral whorl, this the lotus —
behold the marks of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal emperor) visible on the child!'

children.text: yo 'sau svapne tvayā dṛṣṭaś candro devīmukhaṃ viśan /
children.translated_text: 'The moon that was seen by you in a dream entering the queen's face —

children.text: sa evāyam ihotpanna iti mā saṃśayaṃ kṛthāḥ //
children.translated_text: that very one has been born here; have no doubt about it.'
Thus, for those two — <s>Śukanāsa</s> and the king — flooded
with the nectar of joy at seeing [the child], the ocean of delight swelled even more.
Meanwhile, a door-keeper, arriving from the minister's house,
announced the celebration of the birth of a son in <s>Śukanāsa</s>'s household.
The king then repeatedly embraced <s>Śukanāsa</s>
and himself snatched away his upper garment as a gift of congratulation.

children.text: uvāca cainaṃ paśyedaṃ sukhasyopari naḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: And he said to him: 'Behold this — joy upon joy for us!

children.text: ime te patitāḥ satyaṃ tuhine somaraśmayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Truly, the moonbeams have fallen upon your frost [of delight].
Well has the Creator arranged this, conforming to the wishes of both of us,

children.text: sahaiva pātratāṃ nītau yad āvāṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ //
children.translated_text: that we two have been made equal vessels of happiness and sorrow together.'
Then, with the sounds of musical instruments, dances, the clapping of <s>carcarī</s> rhythms,
with powders of <s>sindūra</s> (vermillion) and <s>ghanasāra</s> (camphor), and pastes of <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron),
unrestrained revelry, heedless of distinctions of high and low,
commenced there at the great festival of the royal household.

children.text: rājā tu svagṛhe kelivimardaṃ vīkṣya tādṛśam /
children.translated_text: The king, having witnessed such tumultuous merrymaking in his own house,
went to <s>Śukanāsa</s>'s house and had it doubled.
When the birth-rites and other [ceremonies] were performed, and the sixth-night vigil was completed,
when <s>Vilāsavatī</s> had bathed, and the auspicious time had arrived,
on a day declared propitious by the astrologers, the king,
having bathed and worshipped the foremost <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with a hundred thousand gold [coins],

children.text: sa bhūṣaṇāni vāsāṃsi varṣan parijane śiśoḥ /
children.translated_text: showering ornaments and garments upon the child's retinue,
bestowed the name <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, consonant with [his] dream.
<s>Śukanāsa</s> too, having worshipped the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in a manner befitting <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
gave his own son the name <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>.
Growing gradually, with the tonsure and other auspicious rites duly performed,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> became the supreme ornament of his parents' lap.
With a form lovely as the moon, with sweet childish prattlings,

children.text: avyaktavarṇair ālāpair aharat sa tayor manaḥ //
children.translated_text: and with babblings of indistinct syllables, he stole their hearts.
When the seventh year arrived, the king had a school built
for <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, many times [finer than others], outside the city.
And having had the <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread ceremony) performed at the time proper for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class,
the king placed him there for the attainment of learning.
He appointed teachers skilled in logic and grammar,
experts in the science of archery, and proficient in political science and the like.
<s>Śukanāsa</s> too, having initiated his son according to the prescribed rites,
made him an attendant of the prince, residing in the school.

children.text: nṛpatis tv agamad draṣṭuṃ putraṃ gurukule sthitam /
children.translated_text: The king went to see his son dwelling in the guru's abode,

children.text: prārthito 'pi sa tanmātrā nainam ānāyayad gṛham //
children.translated_text: but even when requested by his mother, he did not have the child brought home.
Then, when he had completed sixteen years, the prince, of keen intellect,
grasped the sciences when taught only once, as if he had studied them before.
Knowing the true meaning of all treatises, a fine poet in all languages,
he became a speaker in all debates, learned in all sciences.

children.text: prauḍhaḥ kalāsu sarvāsu dakṣaḥ sarveṣu karmasu /
children.translated_text: Accomplished in all arts, skillful in all tasks,
in all matters of conduct he was unfailing in his course.

children.text: krameṇa vardhamānaś ca sa vyāyāmam asevata /
children.translated_text: Growing gradually, he devoted himself to physical exercise,
and he shone with the bodily grace acquired through that practice.
With long arms, broad shoulders, a wide chest, a slender waist,
deep-set arms, round thighs — the youth had the noble gait of an elephant.
The son of <s>Śukanāsa</s> was like his reflection,
in all qualities alike, except for the distinction of body and life-breath.

children.text: rājā tu taṃ sutaṃ buddhvā kṛtārthaṃ guruveśmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king, having understood that his son had completed his studies at the guru's house,
at the words of <s>Śukanāsa</s>, proceeded to bring him home.
Having summoned the commander of the army named <s>Balāhaka</s>,
on an auspicious day, having performed the rites, he sent him to bring the prince.
A thousand princes, well-trained and mighty of arm,
he also dispatched along with him, as attendants of the prince.
Likewise, he sent a steed named <s>Indrāyudha</s>,
which had surpassed <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> with its incomparable qualities.
Then <s>Balāhaka</s>, having gone, saw the prince
residing in the school, and bowed to him with respect.

children.text: ācacakṣe ca rājājñāṃ gṛham āgamyatām iti /
children.translated_text: He conveyed the king's command: 'Let him come home,'
and presented to him the princes, mentioning their names.
Then, having learned of the weighty qualities such as valor of the one named <s>Balāhaka</s>,
the princes bowed to him, as the immortals [bow] to <s>Purandara</s> (Indra).
Bringing the horse <s>Indrāyudha</s>, which produced the radiance of a rainbow
through the jeweled lights of its trappings, <s>Balāhaka</s> said again:
Mount this jewel among horses, born in <s>Sindhu</s>, not of natural origin,
presented as a gift to the lord [king] by the ruler of <s>Pārasīka</s> (Persia).

children.text: candrāpīḍas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā turaṅgamam anuttamam /
children.translated_text: But <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, seeing that supreme horse,

children.text: paraṃ vismayam āpede ciraṃ caivam acintayat //
children.translated_text: was filled with extreme wonder and reflected for a long time:

children.text: hṛdayaṃ me bravīty evaṃ naiṣa satyaṃ turaṅgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: My heart tells me this: truly this is no [ordinary] horse;

children.text: ko 'pi kenāpi śāpena nūnaṃ turagatāṃ gataḥ //
children.translated_text: surely some being has assumed horse-form through some curse.
This report of its non-natural birth is witness to this surmise;
for indeed <s>Rambhā</s>, the celestial maiden, became a mare through a curse.
Such height could belong to <s>Garutmat</s> (Garuḍa) or to <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>,

children.text: tejasām ākṛter vāpi na sāmānyeṣu vājiṣu //
children.translated_text: or to some [being] of brilliant form — but not to ordinary horses.
Having thus deliberated with his intellect, adorned with
flower garlands, ornaments, and silken garments presented by <s>Balāhaka</s>,
having taken leave of his teachers, blessed by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, praised by bards,
seeing <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> mounted on another horse,

children.text: yo 'si so 'si namas tubhyam ārohātikramas tvayā /
children.translated_text: Whoever you may be, salutations to you; pardon this impropriety of mounting,
— saying thus, he mounted it.
[A tilaka verse]
Having mounted <s>Indrāyudha</s>, like <s>Acyuta</s> (Viṣṇu) upon <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa),

children.text: api trijagatīṃ kṛtsnāṃ mene hastagatām iva //
children.translated_text: he considered even all the three worlds as if held in his hand.
Then, accompanied by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, departing from that dwelling,
surrounded by the princes, he slowly entered the city.

children.text: tam atha purataruṇyo rājamārgeṇa yāntaṃ dadṛśur atulakāntiṃ saudhavātāyanasthāḥ /
children.translated_text: The young women of the city, standing at the windows of their mansions, beheld him of incomparable beauty passing along the royal highway,
abandoning all gravity and modesty, their limbs trembling with excitement, worshipping him with eyes showing the transformations born of love.
Thus ends the second canto of the Kādambarīkathāsāra, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the teacher, the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Jayanta</s>, who is foremost among the most learned scholars.
The third canto.
Having reached the king's gate and dismounting from the horse,
the crown prince, together with the general and <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, entered the royal palace.
Entering into the middle of the assembly, with eyes moist with tears of joy,

children.text: nyastajānuḥ kṣitau mūrdhnā vavande caraṇau pituḥ //
children.translated_text: placing his knees on the ground, he bowed at his father's feet with his head.

children.text: āliliṅga ca taṃ rājā cucumba śirasi kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: The king embraced him and instantly kissed his head;

children.text: grahītum aicchad utsaṅge sa tu bhūmāv upāviśat //
children.translated_text: he wished to take him on his lap, but [the prince] sat down on the ground.

children.text: draṣṭuṃ punaḥ punaḥ spraṣṭum atṛptenāpi bhūbhujā /
children.translated_text: Though the king, insatiable in seeing and touching him again and again,

children.text: visṛṣṭo 'tha kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā mātaraṃ vandituṃ yayau //
children.translated_text: [reluctantly] let him go; after standing for a moment, he went to pay respects to his mother.
Her, whose breasts were flowing with milk from the joy of seeing her son —
having bowed to all his mothers, he delighted them with his salutations.
Having honored the auspicious reception ceremony performed by them,

children.text: śukanāsam atha draṣṭum ayāsīt tasya mandiram //
children.translated_text: he then went to see <s>Śukanāsa</s> at his residence.

children.text: dvāri vājinam utsṛjya praviśya praśrayeṇa tam /
children.translated_text: Leaving the horse at the gate and entering with humility,
he bowed to him as to a father, touching the ground with his head.

children.text: namantam enam utthāpya svayam utthāya sādaram /
children.translated_text: Raising him as he bowed, rising himself respectfully,
<s>Śukanāsa</s> embraced him around the neck, his face covered with goosebumps.
Though urged, <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> did not sit on the beautiful golden seat,
but sat on the ground before him.

children.text: śukanāsaṃ ca muñcantam āsanaṃ svaṃ nyavārayat /
children.translated_text: And he prevented <s>Śukanāsa</s>, who was about to vacate his own seat.

children.text: tatra kṣaṇam iva sthitvā draṣṭum āgān manoramām //
children.translated_text: Having stayed there for a moment, he went to see <s>Manoramā</s>.
Then, having bowed respectfully to her, as to <s>Vilāsavatī</s> [his own mother],
having received manifold blessings, the auspicious one departed.
And just as was <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>'s sequence of meeting and embracing [in his own household],
so too was <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>'s in the two households.

children.text: na kaścana sutasnehe viśeṣaś ca tayor abhūt /
children.translated_text: Nor was there any difference in the affection for a son

children.text: mantriṇo rājaputre vā mantriputra nṛpasya vā //
children.translated_text: between the minister for the prince and the king for the minister's son.
Then <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> went to the great prince's palace,
which had been previously prepared by his father, equipped with all provisions.

children.text: susaṃniveśam ālokya reme tatra cirāya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing its fine layout, he delighted there for a long time,
and he also arranged a stable for <s>Indrāyudha</s> in his own residence.
Then, when he had bathed, applied unguents to his body, eaten, and was comfortably settled,

children.text: mātrā visṛṣṭa āgatya kañcukī tam abhāṣata //
children.translated_text: the chamberlain, sent by his mother, came and said to him:
This maiden named <s>Patralekhā</s> is the daughter of the king of <s>Kulūta</s>,
who by some turn of fate was separated from her father's house.

children.text: bālaiva vardhitā devyā svayam antaḥpure nije /
children.translated_text: As a child she was raised by the queen herself in her own inner apartments;
she is a worthy ground for all your confidence, fit to be at your side.
Thinking thus, she has been sent by the queen; accept her, O prince,
— saying this, he presented the maiden, modest and fair to behold.
[A tilaka verse]

children.text: sā tu tenārpitā kanyā tataḥ prabhṛti taṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: That maiden, assigned to him, from then on served him such

children.text: asevata yathā cāsya nijaṃ cittam ivābhavat //
children.translated_text: that she became as if his own mind.
He appointed her as the keeper of the betel-box,
and was pleased with her qualities — her character, conduct, propriety, and the like.

children.text: kiyatsv api vyatīteṣu divaseṣv atha pārthivaḥ /
children.translated_text: After some days had passed, the king
began preparations for the ceremony of installing his son as crown prince.
Having consulted with <s>Śukanāsa</s> in the fullness of trust,
he commenced the gathering of materials, having performed the auspicious rites.
When the coronation was imminent, <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> came
for an audience, and <s>Śukanāsa</s> spoke to him at length:
Dear one, for one who has mastered the sciences, who is endowed with discipline and good conduct,

children.text: nālpam apy upadeṣṭavyam asti sthiramates tava //
children.translated_text: and whose mind is steadfast, there is not even the slightest need for instruction.

children.text: kiṃ tu lokottarā lakṣmīr abhirāmam idaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: But extraordinary royal fortune, this captivating body,

children.text: navaṃ vayaḥ parā śaktir iti durviṣaho bharaḥ //
children.translated_text: the freshness of youth, and supreme power — these are a burden difficult to bear.
Royal fortune is indeed the supreme cause of the transformation of men;

children.text: viralās te vikārāya na yeṣāṃ tatparigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: rare are those whom its influence does not corrupt.
It nourishes intense heat, destroys plain-speaking,
and breeds hatred among the devoted — the incomparable fever caused by royal fortune.

children.text: na paśyanti na śṛṇvanti nāpekṣante hitāhitam /
children.translated_text: They do not see, they do not hear, they do not consider what is good or harmful —

children.text: na vidmaḥ kiṃ nu ceṣṭante kaṣṭaṃ śrīviplutā narāḥ //
children.translated_text: we do not know what they are doing — alas, men intoxicated by fortune!
In [the thought] that it has come by succession, there is no assurance whatsoever,

children.text: hyo 'pi yatroṣitā lakṣmīs tatraivādya na dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: for the fortune that dwelt somewhere yesterday is not seen there today.
As if afflicted by gout, as if her feet are pierced by thorns,

children.text: lakṣmīr nidhātuṃ śaknoti na kvacin nirbharaṃ padam //
children.translated_text: fortune is unable to place a firm foot anywhere.

children.text: śrīḥ sapatnīm iva dveṣṭi dṛṣṭiṃ satpathavartinīm /
children.translated_text: Fortune hates the vision that walks the righteous path, as [one hates] a co-wife;

children.text: tāṃ vinā yatra tatraiva patanty andhā iveśvarāḥ //
children.translated_text: without that [vision], rulers fall everywhere like the blind.
And rare are the men who advise them on the righteous path;
for they are exploited by rogues who penetrate their hearts.
Into sense-pleasures that are superficially charming, without restraint,
they are driven by those very rogues, who are experts in the sweetness of speech.
And these, deceived by rogues, their minds attached to sense-pleasures,

children.text: akasmāt pralayaṃ yānti gītaraktā mṛgā iva //
children.translated_text: suddenly perish, like deer drawn by song.

children.text: viṣayeṣv atikaṣṭo 'yaṃ viṣayaḥ strīti nāma yaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among sense-pleasures, the most terrible is this one called 'woman';

children.text: jīvaty anyaiḥ kilākṛṣṭas tenākṛṣṭo na jīvati //
children.translated_text: one who is drawn by [other pleasures] lives, but one drawn by this does not live.
One who places no trust in the wicked, whose mind is not immersed in pleasures,

children.text: sādhuṣv abhimukho nityaṃ mahatīṃ śriyam aśnute //
children.translated_text: who always faces the virtuous — such a one enjoys great prosperity.

children.text: sa tvaṃ na vañcyase dhūrtair na sādhubhir upekṣyase /
children.translated_text: You — may you not be deceived by rogues, not neglected by the good;

children.text: yathā na bādhyase kāmaiḥ prayatethās tathā sadā //
children.translated_text: strive always so that you may not be overwhelmed by desires.

children.text: kāmaṃ bhavān prakṛtyaiva dhīraḥ pitrā ca saṃskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, you are by nature steadfast, and refined by your father;
my excessive satisfaction with your virtues makes me loquacious.

children.text: yugarāja dhuraṃ pitrā kalpitām udvaha sthirām /
children.translated_text: O co-ruler, bear firmly the yoke fitted by your father,

children.text: vijitām api cānena punar jaya vasuṃdharām //
children.translated_text: and conquer again this earth, even though it has already been conquered by him.
Having said this, he who was devoted to his welfare fell silent;
and <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> felt as if adorned by his words.
Then, on an auspicious day, having bathed the beloved prince according to the rites and performed the [proper] ceremonies,
the king consecrated him as crown prince.
The celebration of his consecration, even more than the celebration of his birth,
became a joy-enhancer for all the people.
Kings came from all directions, bearing gifts,
and the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were gratified, having received gifts of cows, land, and gold.
On another day, endowed with excellent qualities praised by the astrologers,
the crown prince, by the king's command, set out on a campaign of conquest.
Having performed the departure-sacrifice through the royal priest who knew the rites,
having worshipped the array of weapons and missiles with the elaborate mantras prescribed by the texts,
having had the benedictions performed by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> gratified with abundant gold,
with his mother's tears restrained with effort, having performed the departure-rites,
with all directions made resonant by the sound of conches and kettledrums,
praised loudly by bards, chroniclers, and panegyrists,
having worshipped the deities with offerings of garlands, unguents, lamps, and the like,
Having bowed to his parents and to <s>Śukanāsa</s>, he departed from the palace.
*[A <s>cakkalaka</s> stanza:]*
Then, mounting [the horse] <s>Indrāyudha</s>, hearing the blessings of the townsfolk and the rural people,

children.text: śṛṇvan nagaryāḥ pūrveṇa dvāreṇa niriyāya saḥ //
children.translated_text: He went forth through the eastern gate of the city.
Then, accompanied by kings numbered in thousands, announced by [the herald horse] <s>Balāhaka</s>,
With their resplendent parasols and <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) waving,
He saw <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> on one side, riding a white horse,
And on the other, <s>Patralekhā</s>, standing in a horse-drawn chariot.
On that day, having advanced only a little, he rested at a picturesque encampment
Prepared on the bank of the <s>Siprā</s> river, with lofty arches.
*[A <s>tilaka</s> stanza:]*
Then, on the following day, having risen, adorned with all ornaments,
He set about departing in continuous march, with unparalleled vigor.
Shaking the denizens of the netherworld with his army,
And obscuring the inhabitants of the sky with the dust raised by it,
Humbling the haughty kings and protecting the submissive ones,
Uprooting the defiant and replanting those who had been uprooted,
Reassuring the distrustful, protecting those who sought refuge,

children.text: dasyūn utsādayan daṇḍaiḥ sādhūn saṃmānayan dhanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: Suppressing bandits with punishments, honoring the virtuous with wealth,
Giving villages to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, establishing rows of temples,
Setting forth his own insignia here and there,
In merely three years, up to the limit of the entire ocean-bounded [earth],
He roamed the earth in continuous march, like <s>Māndhātā</s>.
[A <s>kulaka</s> stanza:]

children.text: jigāya prathamaṃ prācīṃ diśaṃ tadanu dakṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: He conquered first the eastern quarter, then the southern,
Then the western, and afterward the northern — that treasury of valor.
Then, having conquered <s>Suvarṇapura</s>, the abode of the <s>Kirātas</s> (mountain tribes)

children.text: sa suvarṇapuraṃ jitvā daṇḍaṃ jagrāha helayā //
children.translated_text: Called <s>Hemajaṭā</s>, he collected tribute with ease.
And in that exceedingly beautiful land within the borders of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
Wearied from the conquest of the quarters, he rested for some years.

children.text: ekadā tu sa tatsthānād āruhyendrāyudhaṃ vane /
children.translated_text: One day, however, from that place, mounting <s>Indrāyudha</s> in the forest,
Having gone out for hunting, he beheld a <s>Kiṃnara</s> couple — a <s>Kiṃnara</s> with his <s>Kiṃnarī</s>.
Gazing at them with curiosity-drawn eyes, [seeing] the horse-faced pair,

children.text: āditsuḥ prerayāmāsa tāv eva prati vājinam //
children.translated_text: Desiring to capture them, he urged his horse directly toward them.
Those two, frightened by the sight of an unfamiliar human, wishing to enter
A cavern of <s>Kailāsa</s>, he pursued with great speed.
By that horse, trained to tremendous speed through practice of heel-spurring,
A distance of five <s>yojanas</s> was traversed.

children.text: tau ca parvatam ārūḍhāv agratas tasya kiṃnarau /
children.translated_text: But those two <s>Kiṃnaras</s> had ascended the mountain ahead of him;
Thereupon he abandoned the desire to capture them from his heart.

children.text: aśaknod anusartuṃ ca kaścit parijano na tam /
children.translated_text: No attendant was able to follow him,
For how could [anyone] follow <s>Indrāyudha</s> at full gallop, even on <s>Garuḍa</s>?
Then, pulling the reins, seeing his body drenched with the sweat of exertion,
And himself alone, and the panting horse,
Surveying that region beyond the reach of mortals,
He smiled to himself and thought with self-reproach —

children.text: aho kim api me maurkhyam asthānābhiniveśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Alas, what folly of mine, to be so obstinately attached to the wrong pursuit!

children.text: yad ātmā bālakeneva vyartham āyāsito mayā //
children.translated_text: I have wearied myself in vain, like a child."

children.text: agṛhītena ko vārthaḥ ko 'rthaḥ prāptena vāmunā /
children.translated_text: "What purpose is served by not capturing [them]? Or what purpose is served by capturing
A pair of <s>Kiṃnaras</s>? — this the fool in me did not consider."
"The path was not examined, as if I rode in a trance,

children.text: na cātra labhyate martyo mama mārgasya deśikaḥ //
children.translated_text: And no mortal guide for my way can be found here."
"This [region] is said to be the boundary of the <s>Bhārata</s> continent,
Close to <s>Kailāsa</s> — what possibility is there of a mortal here?"
"But in this forest, strewn with leaves and grass, there would be hoofprints of the horse;

children.text: na syur yadanusāreṇa yāsyāmi śibiraṃ nijam //
children.translated_text: By following them I shall return to my own camp."
"I shall simply head south, making the best of it;
But this midday hour has arrived,"

children.text: anubhūto 'timātraṃ ca khedas tad iha sāmpratam /
children.translated_text: "And excessive weariness has been experienced. So now,
Having obtained water from somewhere, I shall go on, free from fatigue."

children.text: iti saṃcintya pānīyam anveṣitum itas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, wandering here and there in search of water,
He spied a dense, lush grove of trees.
Then, proceeding along a path congenial to that [grove], refreshed by breezes
Carrying the fragrance of newly-blooming lotuses,
He then beheld a path strewn with lotus-stalk fragments stuck to the feet of rutting elephants,
Which served as an indicator of [nearby] water.
Going by that [path], in the midst of the grove, he saw
A great lake, resembling the ocean, its far shores invisible.
By the mere sight of it, his fatigue vanished from afar,
And reaching the edge of its sandy bank, he dismounted from his horse.
Having unsaddled the horse, [which] rolled on the ground and rose up,
Seized the fresh grass, plunged [into the water] and shook its mane,
He led the horse to the shore of the lake, tied it to a tree,
And cast before it grass cut with his sword.

children.text: svayaṃ sasnau papau vāri bubhuje bisakandalīḥ /
children.translated_text: He himself bathed, drank water, and ate lotus stalks,
Then with his upper garment as a head-covering, he sat down on a flat stone.
*[A <s>tilaka</s> stanza:]*
Then, having rested for a while, on the northern bank of the lake
He heard a sound of music arising — not of human origin.
With his gaze firmly fixed in that direction, his neck raised,
<s>Indrāyudha</s> (i.e., <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>) first listened with ears [shaped] like tightly closed oyster shells.
"From where does this music come in this desolate place?" — thus, with manifest curiosity,

children.text: utthāya candrāpīḍo 'tha tām eva diśam abhyagāt //
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> rose and went toward that very direction.
As he walked playfully, greedy for the sound of music,
The path itself revealed itself to him, even without being asked.
Going [further], not very far away, he beheld a crystal palace,
Laughing as it were, with its rays, at the splendor of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
There, he saw the four-faced Lord (<s>Brahmā</s>), installed on a jeweled pedestal,
And the blessed Lord <s>Umākānta</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and bowed to them.
Then, having taken her seat near the southern form [of the deity],
Playing the <s>vīṇā</s> placed on her lap, producing melodious sounds,
By the radiance of her body, white as <s>kunda</s> flowers, flowing around her,
She appeared like <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself, dwelling in the midst of the ocean of milk,
Or like <s>Rati</s> seeking to revive <s>Anaṅga</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), who had been destroyed by the fire of [<s>Śiva's</s>] wrath,
Propitiating the husband of <s>Pārvatī</s> through her austerities.
Though in the bloom of youth, having acquired the disposition of practiced renunciation,
He beheld a maiden observing the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, upon seeing her, with his mind seized by wonder, [thought:]

children.text: keyaṃ syāt kanyakā nāsyā divyatāṃ prati saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Who might this maiden be? There is no doubt about her divine nature."
*[A <s>cakkalaka</s> stanza:]*

children.text: nāntardhānam iyaṃ gacchen na vā gaganam utpatet /
children.translated_text: "She does not vanish, nor does she fly up to the sky,
Nor does she resort to silence at the sight of a mortal."
Thus pondering, he remained with his body concealed behind a pillar,
Intent on waiting for the conclusion of the song.
*[A <s>tilaka</s> stanza:]*

children.text: sātha gītaṃ samāpayya vinidhāya ca vallakīm /
children.translated_text: She then, having concluded her song and put away the <s>vallakī</s> (lute),
Having bowed to the Moon-crested One (<s>Śiva</s>), addressed <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>.

children.text: atithe svāgataṃ te 'stu saumya viśramyatām iha /
children.translated_text: "Welcome to you, O guest! O gentle one, please rest here.

children.text: prāpto 'si svām imāṃ bhūmim ita āgamyatām iti //
children.translated_text: You have come to your own land — please come this way."

children.text: candrāpīḍas tad ākarṇya bahv ātmānam amanyata /
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, hearing that, thought very highly of himself,

children.text: vrajantīm anu vavrāja devatāvat praṇamya tām //
children.translated_text: And, bowing to her as to a deity, followed her as she walked.
She then entered her hermitage cave, not very far away,
Where animal skins, <s>kuśa</s> grass, gourds, vessels, staff, and water-pot were kept.
There, seated on a deerskin while he sat on a seat of <s>darbha</s> grass,
She asked <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> about his identity, arrival, and so forth.
He narrated everything in detail, just as it had occurred,

children.text: sā ca vijñātavṛttāntā nirjagāma tato bahiḥ //
children.translated_text: And she, having learned his story, went outside.

children.text: gṛhītabhikṣāpātrā ca kṣaṇam āsta taror adhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking the alms-bowl, she sat for a moment beneath a tree;

children.text: āpūryata svayaṃ śīrṇaiḥ phalais tad amṛtopamaiḥ //
children.translated_text: It filled of its own accord with fallen fruits resembling nectar.
Then she invited <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> to partake of them,

children.text: anvatiṣṭhad vacas tasyāḥ sa ca vismayamānadhīḥ //
children.translated_text: And he, his mind full of wonder, obeyed her words.
After he had eaten, she went to a mountain stream nearby
And herself performed the simple ritual of a fruit-meal.

children.text: āgatya ca punas tasminn upaviṣṭā mṛgājine /
children.translated_text: Coming back again and seated on the deerskin,
She spent some time narrating stories about <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>, <s>Ujjayinī</s>, and the like.

children.text: api nāma svavṛttāntaṃ madvad eṣāpi varṇayet /
children.translated_text: "Perhaps she too, like me, would narrate her own story if asked" —

children.text: pṛṣṭety evaṃ kṣaṇaṃ dadhyau candrāpīḍaḥ sakautukaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> pondered for a moment with curiosity.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā cāsyāḥ praśamamadhurām ākṛtiṃ bhāvaśuddhiṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ ca prakṛtisaralaṃ labdhavākyāvakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing her form, serene and lovely in its tranquility, the purity of her character, and her natural, sincere courtesy, having found an opening for conversation,

children.text: ātmodantaṃ niyatam akhilaṃ vakṣyati prārthiteyaṃ candrāpīḍaḥ kṣaṇam atha kṛtapraśnasampratyayo 'bhūt //
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> became confident that, if asked, she would certainly narrate her entire story — and so he resolved to ask.

children.text: iti śrīvipaścidvarāgragaṇyācāryabhaṭṭaśrījayantasūnor abhinandasya kṛtau kādambarīkathāsāre tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third canto of the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the revered teacher <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Jayanta</s>, foremost among the supremely learned.
The Fourth Canto.
He, whose curiosity grew ever more intense through the increasing power of her virtues,
Addressed her in speech that was sweet, modest, and noble.
"Only through the confidence bestowed by your grace
Is this mind of mine directed toward the restlessness of questioning, O revered one."
"This succession of wonders is not the province of eyes such as mine;
May this person be graced by the favor of your narration."
"Among sages, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and others,
Which lineage has been adorned by the blessed lady's auspicious birth?"
"This body composed of the five elements — how does it bear
A whiteness surpassing the luster of the tusks of the elephants of the quarters?"
"And what is the cause of such extreme renunciation in the bloom of youth,
By which such hardship as dwelling in the forest and the like is endured?"
Even as he was speaking thus, shedding large teardrops,
The divine maiden wept, her face covered by her bark garment.
And the mind of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> trembled as he beheld her —

children.text: iyam apy ākṛtir nāma duḥkhair yad abhibhūyate //
children.translated_text: "That even such a form should be overcome by sorrows!"
She, having wept for a long time, wiping her eyes with her bark garment,

children.text: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya vyāhartum upacakrame //
children.translated_text: And drawing a long, hot sigh, began to speak.
"O prince, what use to you is the story of one like me
Whose sole dwelling is sorrow, who is wicked and ill-fated?"
"Yet if your mind is seized by curiosity,

children.text: tad idaṃ varṇyate sarvam ākarṇaya yathākramam //
children.translated_text: Then all this will be narrated — listen in due order."

children.text: suprasiddham idaṃ tāvat tava śrutipathaṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: "This much is well-known, having already reached the range of your hearing:

children.text: yat santy apsaraso nāma surasadmani kanyakāḥ //
children.translated_text: That there exist maidens called <s>Apsarases</s> in the celestial realm."
"And there are fourteen families of them, each established separately,
Originating from <s>Soma</s>, <s>Amṛta</s>, <s>Samīra</s> (Wind), <s>Arka</s> (Sun), and the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>, and others."
"Among those, from the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>, there are two families of <s>Gandharvas</s>.

children.text: kanye munir ariṣṭeti dve dakṣasya babhūvatuḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣa</s> had two daughters named <s>Muni</s> and <s>Ariṣṭā</s>."
"Among them, the lord of the <s>Gandharvas</s> was named <s>Citragratha</s>,
The son of <s>Muni</s>, named <s>Śrutayaśas</s>, elder to <s>Citrasena</s> and others."
"But the eldest among <s>Tumburu</s> and the rest, the son of <s>Ariṣṭā</s>, was accomplished —
The king of <s>Gandharvas</s> named <s>Haṃsa</s>, of celebrated prowess."
"Unstained, innate, undefiled by the blemish of any malice,
Was the love that grew mutually between those two kings of <s>Gandharvas</s>."
"Not very far from here there is a mountain, brilliant with various gems,

children.text: hemakūṭa iti khyātaḥ sa nivāsas tayor dvayoḥ //
children.translated_text: Known as <s>Hemakūṭa</s> — that was the abode of those two."
"On it dwell countless <s>Gandharvas</s>, supported by the pillar of their arms,

children.text: gandharvās tau ca visrambhabhūmir janmadviṣaḥ parā //
children.translated_text: And those two were the supreme refuge of trust for their natural enemies."

children.text: atha yat somasambhūtam ekam apsarasāṃ kulam /
children.translated_text: "Now, in that one family of <s>Apsarases</s> born of <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: gaurī nāmodabhūt kanyā tasmin pratikṛtir vidhoḥ //
children.translated_text: A maiden named <s>Gaurī</s> was born — a replica of the moon."
"The <s>Gandharva</s> king <s>Haṃsa</s> married her, of moon-like radiance;
Thereby she aptly obtained the name 'swan-gaited' in every way."
"Though trust had been long nurtured abundantly in their household life,

children.text: tayor udabhavat sūnur eko 'pi na mahātmanoḥ //
children.translated_text: Not even a single son was born to those two great souls."
"But I alone, the ill-fated, sinful one, a daughter,
Was born to them — the vessel of this burden of sorrow."
Being childless, my father, filled with joy, celebrated my birth
as if it were the birth of a son, having performed grand festivities.
Seeing this complexion of my body, inherited through the lunar lineage,

children.text: cakre varṇānurūpaṃ sa mahāśveteti nāma me //
children.translated_text: my father gave me the name '<s>Mahāśvetā</s>' (the very white), appropriate to my color.
I, a child in my father's house, melodious like a <s>vallakī</s> (lute),
wandered day and night from the lap of one kinsman to another.
Not yet having attained the succession of pairs such as the savoring of passion, attachment, and the like,
I passed my childhood in a state of ease, free from affliction.
[A couplet:]

children.text: atha bālyāt paraṃ prāpam ahaṃ nānārasāspadam /
children.translated_text: Then, beyond childhood, I reached an age that was the abode of manifold sentiments,
the singular dwelling-place of the transformations of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love).
Once, during the delightful days of the spring month,
I came here to bathe in the clear-watered lake, accompanied by my mother.
Seeing the glory of the <s>mādhavī</s> creeper, never seen elsewhere,

children.text: sakhībhiḥ saha paśyantī kānane vyaciraṃ ciram //
children.translated_text: I lingered for a very long time in the forest with my companions.
Then, in a certain spot, I smelled a wonderful fragrance,
never before smelled, which overpowered the scent of all other flowers.
Impelled by the eagerness of curiosity to discover its source,
going not very far from there, I saw a young ascetic boy.
He seemed like <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) untouched
by the flame of <s>Īśāna's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) [third] eye — like the lunar orb unstained by the drop of blemish.
Even though his beauty was [seemingly] contradicted by his girdle, deerskin, and bark-garments,
these produced an even greater captivation of his extraordinary charm.
He had placed behind his ear a certain blossoming branch of an unfamiliar tree;
the fragrance emanating from it I smelled again and again.
I seemed to drink with my eyes, whose lashes were raised by curiosity,
that handsome one, who had come from somewhere, a cascade of the nectar of beauty.
By the one-sided partiality toward beauty alone, heedless of virtues and faults,
I was then brought under the power of the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>).
Then, wishing to withdraw, yet repeatedly impelled by something
due to my own timidity, I approached his vicinity.
'The community of sages is worthy of veneration' — thinking thus, with my gem-earrings swaying,
I offered my obeisance to him, my eyes fixed upon his face.
Then, when I had made my salutation, he too fell within the range
of <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love) — wonderful! Destiny is not to be transgressed.
Then, as if instructed by <s>Smara</s> (love), perceiving his transformation through my intellect,
having gained confidence, I attained the boldness to ask about his identity and origin.
Then I questioned another young ascetic standing nearby,
a fellow <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) of his, of equal radiance and ascetic garb.

children.text: bhagavan kathyatāṃ ko 'yaṃ kimākhyaḥ kim ihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Revered sir, tell me — who is he? What is his name? Why has he come here?

children.text: karṇe ca nihitānena kasyeyaṃ mañjarī taroḥ //
children.translated_text: And whose tree is this blossoming branch that he has placed upon his ear?'
He replied: 'In the world of the gods, there is a sage honored by gods and demons alike,
renowned as <s>Śvetaketu</s>, unmatched in beauty.'
'He once went to bathe in the <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> (lotus) lake;

children.text: nityaṃ saṃnihitā tatra lakṣmīr enaṃ vyalokayat //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who is always present there, beheld him.'
'She, merely by seeing him — as if by an embrace —
attained fulfillment in the lotus that had become her seat.'

children.text: udapādi tadaivāsya kumāraḥ sa tayā śriyā /
children.translated_text: 'At that very moment, a son was born to him from that <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>);

children.text: tava putro 'yam ity uktvā nyavedi śvetaketave //
children.translated_text: saying "This is your son," she informed <s>Śvetaketu</s>.'

children.text: so 'pi yogadṛśā dṛṣṭvā yathāvat sutam agrahīt /
children.translated_text: 'He too, having seen [the child] with his yogic vision, duly accepted his son

children.text: nāma janmocitaṃ cāsya puṇḍarīka iti vyadhāt //
children.translated_text: and gave him the name <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, fitting for his birth.'
'He initiated him with the sacraments proper to the ascetic community,

children.text: atīte bālabhāve ca nyayuṅkta tapase pitā //
children.translated_text: and when his childhood had passed, his father set him to austerities.'

children.text: ayaṃ sa puṇḍarīkas te varṇitaḥ śṛṇu mañjarīm /
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> has been described to you; now hear about the blossoming branch.
Today being the fourteenth day of the lunar fortnight, he has set out for the temple of <s>Śiva</s>.'
'As he was going, by a forest deity, of her own accord, with the gracious words
"This ornament is equal to your form" —'
'this blossoming branch from the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree, which arose from the churning of the milk-ocean,
was taken and placed upon his ear, even against his will.'
[A couplet:]

children.text: iti tasmin vadaty eva capale gṛhyatām iyam /
children.translated_text: 'Even as that rash one was still speaking, [<s>Puṇḍarīka</s> said]: "Take this!

children.text: kim anena tava praśnalobhenety abhidhāya mām //
children.translated_text: What use is this curiosity of your questioning?" — and saying this to me,'
'that blossoming branch of the celestial tree was brought by that sage,
removed from his own ear, and made into an ear-ornament for mine.'
[A couplet:]
'His fingers trembling from the touch of my cheek-surface,

children.text: tena praskhalitā hastād akṣamālā na lakṣitā //
children.translated_text: the prayer-bead rosary slipped from his hand, unnoticed by him.'

children.text: aprāptaiva ca sā bhūmiṃ gṛhītā sahasā mayā /
children.translated_text: 'Before it even reached the ground, I quickly seized it.
At that moment, the parasol-bearer addressed me:'

children.text: snātā devī ciraṃ bhartṛdārike gamyatām iti /
children.translated_text: '"The queen has finished bathing; O princess, let us go."'

children.text: tataḥ pratinivṛttāyāṃ mayi taṃ sa sakhāvadat //
children.translated_text: 'Then, when I had turned back, his companion said to him:',

children.text: vayasya kim idaṃ cetas tava viplutam īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: '"Friend, what is this? Your mind has become so disturbed!"'

children.text: hṛtām apy anayājñāsīr akṣamālāṃ na kanyayā //
children.translated_text: '"You did not even notice that the maiden took away your rosary!"'

children.text: hṛtā nāmeyam anayā hṛdayaṃ nanu rakṣyatām /
children.translated_text: '"Taken indeed by her! Let the heart at least be guarded!"'
'Then he came again and said, as if in feigned anger:'

children.text: apahṛtyākṣamālāṃ me kva cauri nanu gamyate /
children.translated_text: '"Having stolen my rosary, where are you going, O thief?"'

children.text: atha mandaṃ vihasyeva mayāsya nihitā kare //
children.translated_text: 'Then, gently laughing as it were, I placed it in his hand —'
'saying "Here, releasing the rosary" — but it was my own pearl-necklace from my neck.'
'And even that was not noticed by him, whose gaze was fixed upon my face.'
[A couplet:]

children.text: sakhībhir api me dṛṣṭam idaṃ cāpalam ity aham /
children.translated_text: 'Since my companions too had witnessed this flirtation, I,
feeling somewhat embarrassed, came to the shore of the lake.'

children.text: atrāham asvatantraiva kṣaṇaṃ snātvā yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: 'Here, no longer self-possessed, having bathed briefly and perfunctorily,
I went home with my mother, meditating upon his qualities.'
'Having gone and dismissed all my companions, saying "I am unwell,"
I entered the house alone and sat there, dazed and stupefied by bewilderment.'

children.text: kva gatāsmi kim uktāsmi tena ko 'sāvahaṃ ca kā /
children.translated_text: 'Where had I gone? What had I said to him? Who was he and who was I?

children.text: kim idaṃ kaḥ prakāro 'yam iti nājñāsiṣaṃ tadā //
children.translated_text: What was this? What kind of state was this? I could not understand anything then.'
'After just a moment, my beloved [attendant] named <s>Taralikā</s>,
who carried my betel-box, entered and said this:'

children.text: karṇe munikumāreṇa kṛtā te yena mañjarī /
children.translated_text: '"The young ascetic who placed the blossoming branch upon your ear —
when you had departed, I was asked by him about your identity."'

children.text: tacchrutvā ca svayaṃ tena likhitvā vastrapaṭṭikā /
children.translated_text: '"And having heard [my reply], he himself wrote upon a strip of cloth
and gave it to me, saying: 'Give this to her when she is alone.'"'

children.text: tatas taralikāyās tāṃ hastād ādāya paṭṭikām /
children.translated_text: 'Then, taking that strip of cloth from <s>Taralikā's</s> hand,

children.text: tasyāṃ tu likhitām āryām imām aham avācayam //
children.translated_text: I read aloud this <s>āryā</s> verse written upon it:'
'"Being enticed from afar by a pearl-garland, white as a lotus-stalk,

children.text: haṃsa iva darśitāśo mānasajanmā tvayā nītaḥ //
children.translated_text: like a swan shown [false] hope, my mind, born in <s>Mānasa</s> lake, has been led away by you."'
'But that verse, though an <s>āryā</s>, seemed like a non-<s>āryā</s> (ignoble), further increasing
the delusion of my mind, like a dark night for one suffering from blindness.'

children.text: vada tena kim uktāsi sa kim uktas tvayāpi vā /
children.translated_text: '"Tell me, what did he say to you? What did you say to him?
And how long did you remain confidently near him?"'

children.text: itthaṃ taralikāṃ tat tad ālapantī punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus addressing <s>Taralikā</s> about this and that, again and again,
I somehow passed a portion of the day, as if maddened.'
'Then, as the sun was sinking low, the door-keeper entered',
'and informed me: "Of the two young ascetics whom the princess saw,'
'one of them stands at the gate."'
'"Quickly, let him in!" I said, suspecting [who it might be].'

children.text: sā ca praveśayāmāsa tasya taṃ sahacāriṇam /
children.translated_text: 'She admitted his companion.'
'I honored him with appropriate hospitality and devotion.'
'After resting for a moment on the couch that I had provided,
his two feet wiped clean with my own upper garment,'

children.text: dṛṣṭiṃ taralikāyāṃ sa vaktukāmaḥ kṣaṇaṃ nyadhāt /
children.translated_text: 'he cast his gaze upon <s>Taralikā</s> for a moment, wishing to speak;

children.text: mayā so 'jñāyi pṛṣṭas tu lajjamāna ivābhyadhāt //
children.translated_text: this was understood by me, and when questioned, he spoke as if bashfully:'

children.text: ahaṃ kapiñjalo nāma tasya bālasuhṛn muneḥ /
children.translated_text: '"I am <s>Kapiñjala</s> by name, a childhood friend of that sage.',

children.text: na vāk pravartate me 'sminn anabhyasta ivādhvani //
children.translated_text: 'My speech does not come forth on this path, as though I were unaccustomed to it.'

children.text: kvāyaṃ munijanaḥ śāntaḥ kva cāmī rāgavibhramāḥ /
children.translated_text: '"How [incongruous are] these peaceful ascetics and these tumults of passion!
Yet this endeavor follows from the compulsion of a friend's affection."'

children.text: tad ucyate prayātāyāṃ rājaputri tadā tvayi /
children.translated_text: '"So let it be told: when you had departed, O princess,

children.text: haste muktāvalīṃ bibhrat sa madantikam āgataḥ //
children.translated_text: he came to me, holding the pearl-necklace in his hand."'
'"Ah, what a lovely rosary you have brought!" — with these words at that very moment,

children.text: vihasya sa mayā noktaḥ kiñcic cintopaśāntaye //
children.translated_text: he was told jokingly by me, for some relief from his anxiety.'
'"There was no mode of counsel that [I did not try], no elaboration of examples,

children.text: na so 'sty upāyo mantro vā yo mayā nābhyadhīyata //
children.translated_text: no stratagem or sacred formula that was not employed by me."'
'"Tormented by my words, with his head bowed in shame,

children.text: kṣaṇam antarhito mattaḥ sutarāṃ mām apīḍayat //
children.translated_text: he disappeared from me for a moment, which greatly distressed me."'
