children.text: kṛcchrād iva mayā labdho vicitya sakalaṃ vanam /
children.translated_text: '"Found by me with great difficulty after searching the entire forest,

children.text: anya eva sa saṃvṛtto vacasāṃ yo na gocaraḥ //
children.translated_text: he had become utterly another person, beyond the reach of words."'
'"Seeing him in that state, having lost hope of bringing him to his senses,
I became devoted to effort for the preservation of his life, as follows:"'
'"Having spread a bed of lotus-leaves sprinkled with sandalwood,
I scattered <s>karpūra</s> (camphor) powder on his limbs as he lay there."'

children.text: trapayā tadavastho 'pi sa kiñcid vaktum akṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"Even in that condition, he was unable to say anything due to shame;
he cast upon me a pitiful gaze, dimmed with tears."'
'"Then I thought: this alone is timely here —
O princess, I have come as a gift for the life of a friend."'

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ tu sāmarthyagatārthā mama yā giraḥ /
children.translated_text: '"Beyond this, the words that revolve in my throat,

children.text: kaṇṭhe viparivartante nūnaṃ tvam api vettha tāḥ //
children.translated_text: their purpose accomplished by implication — surely you too understand them."'

children.text: iti tasmin vadaty eva praviśya prāha kañcukī /
children.translated_text: 'Even as he was speaking thus, a chamberlain entered and said:',
'"Knowing that you are unwell, the queen has come."'
'Hearing that, <s>Kapiñjala</s>, fearful of the crowd of people, departed;

children.text: na sa prativacaḥ kiñcin māmakīnam apaikṣata //
children.translated_text: he did not wait for any reply from me.'

children.text: taduktāṃ tu daśāṃ tasya janasyāvetya tādṛśīm /
children.translated_text: 'But having learned the condition of that [<s>Puṇḍarīka</s>], as described by him,

children.text: āgatāṃ nāgatāṃ vāpi nāham ambām alakṣayam //
children.translated_text: I did not notice whether my mother had come or not.'

children.text: tataḥ kamalinīṃ raktāṃ tyaktvā kvāpi gate ravau /
children.translated_text: 'Then, when the sun had gone somewhere, abandoning the reddened lotus,
and when the inauspicious moon had risen, bringing only distress —'
'as if uprooted by <s>Kāma</s> (love), as if burned by the fire of separation,
I spoke again to <s>Taralikā</s> alone, my voice choked with tears:'

children.text: ahaṃ yathā tathā vāpi bhaveyaṃ sa tu matkṛte /
children.translated_text: '"However I may be, let that be — but how will he fare on my account?

children.text: kathaṃ bhaviṣyatīty eṣā cintā dalayatīva mām //
children.translated_text: This worry seems to split me apart."'
'"On one side: scripture, family custom, modesty, and fear of elders;

children.text: itaḥ kāmo vasanto 'pi viraho maraṇād bhayam //
children.translated_text: on the other: love, and spring, and separation, and the fear of death."'

children.text: vada kiṃ karavāṇy atra muhyatīva mano mama /
children.translated_text: '"Tell me, what should I do? My mind seems to reel.

children.text: mā bhūn me varake vipraprāṇabādhena majjanam //
children.translated_text: Let there not be, for wretched me, a drowning caused by harming a brahmin's life!"'
'As I was lamenting thus, a swoon, easily arising at that time,
robbed me of consciousness, as sleep robs the luster from the eyes.'
'Then, having revived me with cool water and breezes,
<s>Taralikā</s>, falling at my feet with tear-filled eyes, said:'

children.text: kiṃ śāstraṃ guravaḥ ke ca kā lajjā kā kulasthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: '"What is scripture? Who are elders? What is modesty? What is family tradition?

children.text: rakṣyantām ātmanaḥ prāṇā yūnas tasya ca sarvathā //
children.translated_text: Let the lives of both — yours and that young man's — be preserved by all means!"'
'"This <s>gāndharva</s> form of marriage — the union of two by mutual desire —

children.text: śāstreṣu paṭhitas tasmāt tūrṇam uttiṣṭha gamyatām //
children.translated_text: is prescribed in the scriptures; therefore quickly arise, let us go!"'
'Thus urged by her, having assumed attire appropriate to the occasion, from the house,

children.text: tām ekām agrataḥ kṛtvā nirgatāham alakṣitā //
children.translated_text: placing her alone ahead, I went out unnoticed.'
'I came to this place with steps quickened by eagerness;

children.text: tadā me dakṣiṇaṃ cakṣur aspandata muhur muhuḥ //
children.translated_text: at that time, my right eye throbbed repeatedly.'
'And I indistinctly heard the sound of weeping in the forest;
alarmed by that, I went with even greater haste.'
'Having gone a few steps — "Ah, dear friend, O treasury of austerity!

children.text: puṇḍarīka kva yāto 'si śūnyaṃ kṛtvā jagattrayam //
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>! Where have you gone, leaving the three worlds empty?"'

children.text: hā hato 'smi vilīno 'smi dagdho 'smi karavāṇi kim /
children.translated_text: '"Ah, I am slain! I am dissolved! I am burned! What shall I do?

children.text: gatvā tātasya vakṣyāmi śvetaketoḥ kim agrataḥ //
children.translated_text: What shall I say, having gone before his father <s>Śvetaketu</s>?"'
'"O wicked <s>Mahāśvetā</s>! Were you not satisfied with the rosary?

children.text: hṛtā me suhṛdo 'muṣya prāṇavṛttir api tvayā //
children.translated_text: You have stolen even the means of life from this friend of mine!"'

children.text: vayasya dehi me vācaṃ na jīvāmi tvayā vinā /
children.translated_text: '"Friend, give me your voice! I shall not live without you!"
Then I heard <s>Kapiñjala</s> lamenting thus and more.'
[A <s>cakkalaka</s> verse:]
'Then, my limbs trembling, my steps faltering,
as if lifted and carried by some [unseen force], I reached that spot.'
'Going there, I saw him — his life departed at that very moment.'
"Why have you come so late?" — as if angry, it stood thus.

children.text: etāvad uktvā mūrchādhiṃ svavṛttāntam ataḥ param /
children.translated_text: Having said this much, on the verge of a swoon, her story from this point onward —
as if wishing to tell it, that maiden fell upon the stone surface.
And <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, beholding her with her consciousness lost,
considered himself — the questioner — to be one who had committed an offense.
Rising hastily, with the breezes from plantain leaves

children.text: toyaiś ca śiśirasvacchaiḥ saṃjñām enām ajigrahat //
children.translated_text: and with cool, clear waters, he revived her consciousness.

children.text: avāpya cetanām eṣā smṛtvā tadvyasanaṃ nijam /
children.translated_text: Having recovered her awareness, she, recalling her own calamity,
as if experiencing it anew, wept and lamented.

children.text: tarūṇām apy abhajyanta hṛdayāni tadā śucā /
children.translated_text: Even the hearts of the trees were broken by grief at that time;
the directions too seemed to weep aloud, as if through echoes.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> then said to her, his eyes choked with tears:

children.text: āstāṃ na śakyate vaktuṃ śrotuṃ cānyad ataḥ param //
children.translated_text: "Enough — nothing beyond this can be spoken or heard."

children.text: katham apy upasaṃhṛtya śokāvegaṃ tu sāvadat /
children.translated_text: But somehow restraining the rush of grief, she said:

children.text: kim ataḥ param asty anyad vācyaṃ śrotavyam eva vā //
children.translated_text: "What else is there to say or indeed to hear beyond this?
But I shall tell you the wonder by which slender thread of hope,

children.text: rājaputra bibharmīdaṃ tad āścaryaṃ bravīmi te //
children.translated_text: though my life is destroyed, I sustain this [existence], O prince!"
"At that time, for such an extremely intense burden of suffering,
no remedy other than death was grasped by me."
"And when I had become resolute in my determination to die and had made preparations,

children.text: niriyāya ca candramaṇḍalāt puruṣaḥ ko 'pi himopamadyutiḥ //
children.translated_text: some person of moon-like radiance emerged from the orb of the moon."

children.text: so 'vatīrya gaganān mahītale taṃ nidhāya bhujapañjarāntare /
children.translated_text: "He, descending from the sky to the earth and placing him within the cage of his arms,

children.text: utpatan divam udārayā girā mām avocata piteva sāntvayan //
children.translated_text: ascending again to the heavens, spoke to me with a noble voice, consoling me like a father:"

children.text: virama maraṇodyogād asmāt priyeṇa tavāmunā punar api mahāśvete vatse bhaviṣyati saṃgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "'Desist from this effort at death — with this beloved of yours, O child, there will again be a reunion at <s>Mahāśveta</s>.'"

children.text: iti giram ahaṃ tasmāc chrutvā sasambhramavismayā kim idam iti taṃ tatrāpṛcchaṃ prasṛtya kapiñjalam //
children.translated_text: "Hearing this speech from him, I, filled with agitation and wonder, asked him 'What is this?' — reaching out toward <s>Kapiñjala</s>."
"'Where are you going now, having carried off my dear friend?' — with eyes raised, trembling with fierce and terrible anger,

children.text: mama vacanam adattvā kiñcid evātivegā kṛtaparikarabandhaḥ so 'py agād antarikṣam //
children.translated_text: without giving any answer to my words, with extreme speed, having girded himself, he too departed into the sky."

children.text: paśyantyāṃ mayi te trayo 'pi viviśuḥ śītatviṣo maṇḍalaṃ tatsampratyayasaṃhṛtocitavidhiḥ sāhaṃ śritedaṃ vratam /
children.translated_text: "As I watched, all three entered the orb of the cool-rayed moon; and I, with the proper rites concluded by that assurance, adopted this vow.

children.text: tātenaitya tataḥ prabhṛty aham ihāsīnātha netuṃ gṛhaṃ yatnenāpi na pāriteti suciraṃ sthitvā gataḥ svān gṛhān //
children.translated_text: Thereafter my father, having come here and tried with effort to take me home but failing, remained for a long time and then returned to his own dwelling."

children.text: iti śrīvipaścidvarāgragaṇyācāryabhaṭṭaśrījayantasūnor abhinandasya kṛtau kādambarīkathāsāre caturthaḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth canto in the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the teacher <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Jayanta</s>, who is foremost among the learned.
The Fifth Canto
Thus, having disclosed at length the honest account of her own history,
<s>Mahāśvetā</s> fell silent, her lip withered by sighs.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, however, meditating upon the stirring of love,
though trembling with wonder within, spoke to her consolingly:
"By me, who despite long observation could see no resolution [to your suffering],
your grief has been renewed, [as I listened] with a mind overcome by curiosity."

children.text: sā tvamarhasi kalyāṇi na śokaṃ kartum īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: "But you, O auspicious one, should not grieve so;
you have surely been consoled by the moon-god himself."
"Who else of such appearance and such power, emerging from that orb

children.text: nirgatya tatraiva viśan niśi sambhāvyate naraḥ //
children.translated_text: and re-entering it — what other man can be imagined at night?"
"Wondrous movements of the gods are heard of in many ways,
fashioned by the variety of boons, curses, the power of austerity, and <s>yoga</s>."
"And <s>Śvetaketu</s>, her father, stands equal to <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: nāsty eva tasya tapasām asādhyaṃ nāma kiñcana //
children.translated_text: there is truly nothing that is beyond the reach of his austerities."
With such logical arguments and illustrations from ancient history,

children.text: mahāśvetāṃ samāśvāsya punaḥ papraccha tām asau //
children.translated_text: having consoled <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, he then asked her again:

children.text: sā te taralikā nāma visrambhanibhṛtā sakhī /
children.translated_text: "That confidential and trusted friend of yours named <s>Taralikā</s> —

children.text: gatā bhagavati kvādya na hi sā tvāṃ vimuñcati //
children.translated_text: where has she gone today, O blessed one? For she never leaves you."
Then <s>Mahāśvetā</s> said: "Where would that poor woman go?

children.text: śṛṇvannāpi nimittaṃ te yathā sā prahitā mayā //
children.translated_text: Hear the reason for which she was sent by me, even as you listen."
"That <s>Gandharva</s> king named <s>Citraratha</s>, whom I described,
by whom even the great lord <s>Maheśvara</s> was worshipped —"

children.text: yena khānitam atyaccham acchodākhyam idaṃ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: "By whom this lake called <s>Acchoda</s>, supremely clear, was dug,

children.text: yena caitrarathaṃ nāma kṛtam etac ca kānanam //
children.translated_text: and by whom this forest called <s>Caitraratham</s> was made —"
"His queen, born in the family of <s>Apsarases</s> sprung from nectar,

children.text: mahiṣī madirā nāma jīvitād api vallabhā //
children.translated_text: named <s>Madirā</s>, dearer to him than life itself."
"They have a daughter named <s>Kādambarī</s>, in the bloom of youth,
as if mocking <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself with the charm of her beauty and grace."

children.text: tayā saha mahat prema bālyāt prabhṛti me tathā /
children.translated_text: "My love for her has been so great since childhood

children.text: yathaikam eva jānāti jano jīvitam āvayoḥ //
children.translated_text: that people know our lives as one."
"Having learned of this wretched account of mine,
that young woman took a vow, though restrained by her kinsmen:"
"'As long as <s>Mahāśvetā</s> does not find an end to this suffering,

children.text: tāvan mayā na kartavyaṃ pāṇigrahaṇam ātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: so long I shall not accept marriage for myself.'"

children.text: ato yathā yathā tasyā yauvanaśrīr vijṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, the more her youthful beauty blossoms,

children.text: tathā tathā tato dhatte khedaṃ citrarathaḥ param //
children.translated_text: the more extreme anxiety <s>Citraratha</s> feels."

children.text: saṃdiṣṭaṃ tena me putri yatasvāvahitā tathā /
children.translated_text: "He has sent me a message: 'O daughter, make such an effort
that your sister is released from this difficult-to-loosen knot.'"
"Therefore I have sent <s>Taralikā</s> there with many instructions

children.text: prahitā bahu saṃdiśya śvaś cāganteha sā punaḥ //
children.translated_text: appropriate to the occasion, and she will return here tomorrow."
Thus, having spent the day in <s>Mahāśvetā</s>'s hermitage with this story,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, when the sun had set, performed the twilight rites.
There, having brought <s>Indrāyudha</s> [his horse] and tethered him in a thicket,
he prepared a bed of leaves in the place indicated by <s>Mahāśvetā</s>.
Though seated upon it and fatigued, he spent a long time

children.text: kathām āścaryabahulāṃ tām eva dhyāyataś ciram //
children.translated_text: meditating upon that very tale, full of wonders, as he had heard it.

children.text: punaś cintayataḥ senāṃ vaiśampāyanam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Again thinking of his army and of <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>

children.text: pattralekhāṃ ca sā rātrir gatā prāyeṇa jāgrataḥ //
children.translated_text: and of <s>Pattralekhā</s>, that night passed mostly in wakefulness.
<s>Indrāyudha</s> the horse, however, gazed with tears in his eyes
upon <s>Mahāśvetā</s>'s face with recognition, intensely, as if human.
When the night had passed and the morning rites had been performed,
knowing that <s>Mahāśvetā</s> had risen from meditation, he went to her presence.
When <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> had entered, with the sun not yet risen far,
<s>Taralikā</s> then arrived, accompanied by <s>Gandharva</s> princes.
She, having entered and bowed to <s>Mahāśvetā</s> and then sat down,
when asked 'Was your mission successful?', spoke with a tilted neck:
"Hear from the mouth of <s>Keyūraka</s>, who has come at her command,
the truth of what the young princess said upon hearing your message."
Then <s>Keyūraka</s> said: "Are you not already aware of [her] heart?

children.text: svasya svameva cedaṃ te manmanaḥ kiṃ parīkṣase //
children.translated_text: Since this is your own heart reflected, why do you test mine?"
"Or rather, I am the ground for greater reproach,
since you dwell in the forest of austerities while she remains at home."
"Having heard the words of your message from <s>Taralikā</s>'s mouth,
this return-message is conveyed by your dear friend."
Hearing this, <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, her eyes motionless for a moment,

children.text: cintayitvā kim apy antaś candrāpīḍam abhāṣata //
children.translated_text: having pondered something inwardly, spoke to <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>:
"O prince, your appearance and your graceful conduct
extend desire in every way even to those who are free from longing."
"If you have heard the words of <s>Kādambarī</s> from <s>Keyūraka</s>,

children.text: tatra ko vā pratīkāraḥ svayaṃ madgamanād ṛte //
children.translated_text: then what remedy is there other than my going there in person?"

children.text: ito na dūre gandharvarājadhānī tadadya tām /
children.translated_text: "Not far from here is the capital of the <s>Gandharva</s> king; today
go and see it at my request — tomorrow you will proceed to your army."
"By showing them your noble and lovely form,
much benefit would be done by me to the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>."

children.text: candrāpīḍas tu tāṃ prāha bahūktvā bhavagaty alam /
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> said to her: "Enough of much talk about destiny;
the command of sages cannot be disobeyed by me."

children.text: prāvartata tato gantuṃ sa mahāśvetayā saha /
children.translated_text: He then set out to go with <s>Mahāśvetā</s>,

children.text: padbhyām eva niyujyāśvaṃ prati keyūrakaṃ dṛśā //
children.translated_text: on foot, directing the horse toward <s>Keyūraka</s> with a glance.
<s>Keyūraka</s>, going ahead, reported to <s>Kādambarī</s>
his coming, his appearance, and his qualities that inspired wonder.

children.text: sa gatvā kiñcid adhvānaṃ candrāpīḍaḥ samāsadat /
children.translated_text: Having traveled a short distance, <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> arrived at
the <s>Gandharva</s> king's city, another <s>Amarāvatī</s> (city of the gods).
Reaching the capital with its tall crystal gateways
and crossing seven enclosures, he entered the inner quarters of the princesses.
Entering by the path indicated by <s>Keyūraka</s>,
he beheld a splendid pavilion with shining pillars of gems.
In the middle of that [pavilion], seated upon a jeweled couch,
surrounded by an abundant, marvelous array of women adorned with gem-ornaments,
making the directions appear as if washed in the brilliance of heated gold,
with the luster of her body outshining the radiance of gems —
softening even a bystander's heart, breaking through even proper conduct,
standing as if within a new, inwardly surging ocean of gracefulness —
having attained the status of being the standard of comparison for all things worthy of comparison —
he beheld <s>Kādambarī</s>, his eyes opened wide with amazement.
Examining within himself the wealth of beauty and grace

children.text: tasyāṃ nirūpayann antar acintayad atha kṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: that stood at the ultimate summit of surpassing excellence, he reflected for a moment:

children.text: satyaṃ na kaścid āścaryanirmāṇeṣv avadhir vidheḥ /
children.translated_text: "Truly, there is no limit to the Creator's capacity for producing wonders,

children.text: īdṛśāny api ratnāni sraṣṭuṃ prabhavati sma yaḥ //
children.translated_text: since he is capable of fashioning gems such as these!"

children.text: moghaṃ yāti hareḥ kālo lakṣmīṃ vakṣasi bibhrataḥ /
children.translated_text: "The time of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who bears <s>Lakṣmī</s> on his chest, passes in vain;
<s>Candraśekhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who bears <s>Gaurī</s> on half his body, has been cheated."
"Even the thousand eyes of <s>Vajrin</s> (<s>Indra</s>), unblinking,

children.text: ananyakarmaṇā yena nityam eṣā na dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: devoted to no other task, can never behold her fully."
As he was thinking thus, the daughter of <s>Citraratha</s>
rose and came forward hastily to welcome <s>Mahāśvetā</s>.
<s>Mahāśvetā</s>, embracing her fearlessly with an embrace full of affection,
spoke to her with <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>'s introduction first:

children.text: ayaṃ hi bhārate varṣe sārvabhaumasya bhūpateḥ /
children.translated_text: "This one, in the land of <s>Bhārata</s>, is the son of the emperor,
the sovereign <s>Tārāpīḍa</s> — <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> has come here."
"By his entering here and coming within the range of sight,
let there be a great festival for the entire <s>Gandharva</s> household!"
Then <s>Kādambarī</s> cast upon him a long gaze
that blossomed with the lifting of her eyelashes and extended its sidelong glance to the ears.
And through that very opened door, by his own <s>māyā</s> (enchantment),
<s>Madana</s> (the god of love) entered within her and established his foothold in her heart.
When <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> had taken his seat on a jeweled stool nearby,
the daughters of the swan and <s>Citraratha</s> shared a single conversation.
Then <s>Mahāśvetā</s> forcibly made <s>Kādambarī</s>, who sat motionless with shyness,
perform the hospitality rites for <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>.
<s>Kādambarī</s>'s dear friend, inseparable from her very body,
named <s>Madalekhā</s>, performed the washing of his feet.
<s>Kādambarī</s>, with her sprout-like hands trembling with perspiration,
under the pretense of [offering] betel, offered herself to him.
Her mind stolen by the sweetness of the touch of his fingertips,
she did not notice the jeweled bracelet slipping from her hand.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> too, through the wealth of bliss from the touch of her hand,
then considered himself the lord of all three worlds.
Then, while the entire company of maidens sat in silence,
there arose a quarrel between a parrot and a mynah bird, a cause for amusement.
And in that connection, to increase their quarrel, with a smile,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> spoke [such words] that all the women laughed.
And those [women], the quarters washed by the radiance of their teeth, with sweet voices,
stole <s>Kādambarī</s>'s heart all the more through [the charm of] <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>'s words.
After but a moment had passed, a chamberlain entered and said:

children.text: rājaputryau yuvāṃ draṣṭuṃ devī nirvighnam icchati //
children.translated_text: "O princesses, the queen wishes to see you both without hindrance."
Having seated <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> comfortably in a crystal mansion
on a pleasure-hill, they went to the presence of the mother.
There, with <s>Keyūraka</s> leading the way, the chief companions of <s>Kādambarī</s>
attended upon <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, who was seated on a couch.
He performed the rituals of bathing, anointing, and eating,
furnished with provisions worthy of the city of the immortals, offered by them.

children.text: atha mandaprabhe bhānau bheje kādabarī nijam /
children.translated_text: Then, when the sun grew dim, <s>Kādambarī</s> ascended to the top of
her own great palace, with only <s>Madalekhā</s> as her companion.
And from there, she gazed at <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, who was upon the pleasure-hill,
with a glance whose sidelong rays extended to the full length of her eyes.
At that moment, upon <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> fell her sharp-pointed sidelong glances,
and upon her fell the arrows of the flower-armed god (<s>Kāma</s>) simultaneously.
And brought together swiftly by their converging sidelong glances,
as if drinking his beauty, she spoke to <s>Madalekhā</s>:

children.text: na mayā madano nāma kathāsvapi sakhi śrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O friend, I had never heard even in stories the name of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love);
today he has been seen before my very eyes, in the form of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>.
<s>Mahāśvetā</s> said nothing about the matter at hand,
and yet by bringing him here, she has said everything without a word.

children.text: api nāma vikāro me tadānīṃ lakṣitas tayā /
children.translated_text: Perhaps my agitation was noticed by her at that time;

children.text: kiṃ vā na lakṣayed eṣā dṛṣṭamanmathavikriyā //
children.translated_text: or how could she, who has witnessed the transformations wrought by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), fail to notice?
Even now, I am trying to withdraw this agitation of mind

children.text: manasaḥ saṃharāmy eva sthūlām api yathātathā //
children.translated_text: which is contrary to my own resolve, however overwhelming it may be.

children.text: kiṃ tv asau śeṣahāro 'syāstulyaṃ maṇḍanam ākṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: But this remaining necklace — an ornament befitting his form —

children.text: urasy anicchato 'py asya tūrṇam āmucyatāṃ tvayā //
children.translated_text: let it be quickly placed by you upon his chest, even against his will.'

children.text: madalekhā gṛhītvā taṃ hāraṃ gatvā tadantike /
children.translated_text: <s>Madalekhā</s>, taking that necklace, went near him

children.text: tathovāca yathā tena pratyuktā sā na kiñcana //
children.translated_text: and spoke in such a way that he replied nothing.
Then the necklace was placed around his neck by <s>Madalekhā</s>,
its radiance filling the quarters like the generous rays of the autumn moon.
And <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, adorned with the necklace, shone
like the full moon encircled by a garland of stars.

children.text: kādambarī ciraṃ tv enam avalokya niśāgame /
children.translated_text: <s>Kādambarī</s>, gazing at him for a long time, as night approached,
descended very slowly from that palace summit.
Then <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, rising and performing the twilight rites,

children.text: avālambata dehena śayyāṃ cintāṃ ca cetasā //
children.translated_text: reclined his body on the bed and his mind on thought.

children.text: kiṃ syur gandharvakanyāyā vilāsāḥ sahajā ime /
children.translated_text: 'Are these innate charms of a <s>Gandharva</s> maiden,

children.text: utemaṃ janam uddiśya bālāṃ nartayati smaraḥ //
children.translated_text: or does <s>Smara</s> (Love) make the young woman dance, directing her toward this person?
Given the way her glance moves about like a skilled messenger-woman,

children.text: tathā sambhāvanā hīyaṃ mama cetasi vartate //
children.translated_text: this very expectation arises in my mind.
I know that the course of pursuit of the <s>Kinnaras</s> (celestial beings) has so far blossomed;

children.text: sa kālapariṇāmena na jāne kiṃ phaliṣyati //
children.translated_text: I do not know what fruit it will bear with the passage of time.
Or rather, this delusion of mine is caused by the intoxication of youth;

children.text: kva mānuṣyaḥ kva gandharva iti kiṃ tena saṃgatam //
children.translated_text: what connection is there between a human and a <s>Gandharva</s>?
And let this self-flattery cease, being of an unseemly nature;

children.text: kālena vyajyate sarvaṃ kathaṃ ca mama sainikāḥ //
children.translated_text: time reveals everything — and besides, what of my soldiers?'
As he pondered thus, sleep, long accumulated,
caused his eyes to close like buds, until the passing of the night.
The next day, having risen and completed his morning routine,
having seen <s>Kādambarī</s> and <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, as if having recovered something long lost,
and having received their permission, accompanied by <s>Gandharva</s> attendants assigned by them,

children.text: sa indrāyudham āruhya pratasthe pṛtanāṃ prati //
children.translated_text: he mounted <s>Indrāyudha</s> (his horse) and set forth toward his army.

children.text: atha kenāpy upāyena labdhamārgam asau nijam /
children.translated_text: Then, by some means having found his way,
he beheld his own camp, encamped on the shore of a lake.

children.text: tatra dṛṣṭvā nṛpān sarvān mantriputraṃ rahasy asau /
children.translated_text: There, having seen all the princes, he privately made the minister's son
aware of his circumstances, and especially <s>Pattralekhā</s>.

children.text: niśi tasyām atītāyām anyedyur udite ravau /
children.translated_text: When that night had passed and the sun had risen the next day,
<s>Keyūraka</s>, having arrived from <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, addressed him:

children.text: kādambarī na paṭvīti tvām abhīṣṇaṃ didṛkṣate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kādambarī</s>, being unable to speak directly, wishes to see you repeatedly,
and has sent the remaining necklace that was forgotten in the bedchamber.'
Hearing <s>Keyūraka</s>'s words, accompanied by <s>Pattralekhā</s>,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> quickly went again to <s>Hemakūṭa</s>.
Having saluted <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, and being praised by her for his arrival,
he then beheld <s>Kādambarī</s>, with <s>Pattralekhā</s> going before him,
seated within a pavilion of ice built upon the bank of the garden lotus-pond,
reclining on a bed of plantain leaves, her body wilted.
Merely by seeing him, she seemed to be repeatedly revived;
then, wishing to rise, she remained lying down at his word.
Then their conversations commenced, purified merely by
polite inquiries about well-being, and moistened with various playful charms.

children.text: tathā tatra ciraṃ sthitvā tāṃ tathā vaśavartinīm /
children.translated_text: Having stayed there for a long time, and seeing her so compliant,
through oblique hints and speeches, he clearly conveyed his own feelings.
At her request, having assigned <s>Pattralekhā</s> to attend upon her,
he, accompanied by <s>Keyūraka</s>, departed again to his camp.
There, observing a letter-bearer who had arrived from <s>Ujjayinī</s> the day before,

children.text: avalokya tadānīṃ taṃ lekhaṃ svayam avācayat //
children.translated_text: he then read the letter himself.
Learning his father's command, which indicated swift return,
he placed the letter in <s>Keyūraka</s>'s hand, his eyes narrowing [with sorrow].

children.text: tadartham atha saṃmantrya saha mantrisutena saḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having deliberated on this matter together with the minister's son,

children.text: evam etad iti dhyāyan prasthānasthairyam agrahīt //
children.translated_text: thinking 'so be it,' he resolved firmly on departure.

children.text: satyaṃ vacmi bhavatprasādarasikaṃ ceto mamaitatpadaṃ gantuṃ necchati kiṃ tu śāsanam idaṃ nollaṅghanīyaṃ guroḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I speak truly — my heart, relishing your grace, does not wish to depart from this place; but this command of my father must not be transgressed;

children.text: manyuḥ samprati sahyatāṃ punar ihāgantāsmi kādambarīṃ saṃdiśyeti sabāṣpagadgadam asau keyūrakaṃ prāhiṇot //
children.translated_text: let the displeasure be borne for now; I shall come here again' — thus instructing <s>Kādambarī</s>, he tearfully and falteringly sent off <s>Keyūraka</s>.

children.text: vaiśampāyanam abhyabhāṣata bhavān saṃvāhayan vāhinīṃ paścād eṣyati yāmi satvaram ahaṃ svalpair ito vājibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: He addressed <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>: 'You shall come later, conducting the army; I shall depart swiftly from here with a few horses' —

children.text: niścityeti tadā prayāṇapaṭahe datte pratasthe tato gatvā kiñcana caṇḍikāśramataṭīm adhyāsta tasmin dine //
children.translated_text: having thus decided, when the march-drum was struck, he departed; and having gone some way, he rested on the bank of the <s>Caṇḍikā</s> hermitage that day.
There, passing the night with diversions of stories about the <s>Draviḍa</s> ascetics' imposing appearance, dress, speech, austerities, and spiritual attainments,

children.text: nītvā niśāṃ satatamaskhalitaprayāṇaiḥ svalpair dinais tvaritamujjayinīmavāpa //
children.translated_text: with ever-uninterrupted marches, in a few days he swiftly reached <s>Ujjayinī</s>.

children.text: iti śrīvipaścidvarāgragaṇyācāryabhaṭṭajayantasūnor abhinandasya kṛtau kādambarīkathāsāre pañcamaḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth canto of the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the teacher, the venerable <s>Jayanta</s>, foremost among the assembly of the most distinguished scholars.
Sixth Canto
Then, having entered the city and attended upon his parents for a long time,
and upon <s>Śukanāsa</s>, he settled again in the prince's palace.
There, with his mind single-pointedly absorbed in meditation upon <s>Kādambarī</s>,

children.text: babhūva rataye nāsya kiñcitsthāsnu cariṣṇu ca //
children.translated_text: nothing, whether stationary or moving, held any delight for him.

children.text: nākarot priyam āhāraṃ nābodhi madhuraṃ rasam /
children.translated_text: He did not relish food, did not perceive sweet flavors,

children.text: na cādriyata vāsāṃsi na siṣeve vilepanam //
children.translated_text: did not care for garments, and did not use fragrant unguents.
Like a traveler separated from his caravan, like an elephant strayed from its herd,
like a deer fawn caught in the meshes of a snare —

children.text: divā vibhāvarīṃ dhyāyan niśi vāñchan dināgamam /
children.translated_text: by day he longed for night, at night he yearned for the coming of day,
ceaselessly gazing toward the northern direction with tear-filled eyes.
'Having learned from <s>Keyūraka</s> and others of my departure, would she still think of me?

children.text: kiṃ vadet pattralekhāṃ vā sāpi kiṃ vocyate tayā //
children.translated_text: What would she say? Or what would <s>Pattralekhā</s> be told by her?'
Thus meditating night and day, without attaining peace,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> passed some considerable time in this manner.

children.text: ākāraḥ saṃvṛtas tv īdṛg asya gūḍhātmano 'bhavat /
children.translated_text: Yet his concealment of his condition was such — his nature being secretive —

children.text: yathā tāṃ śūnyatāṃ tasya pitarau nādhijagmatuḥ //
children.translated_text: that his parents did not discover that inner emptiness.
Then, after some days had passed, <s>Pattralekhā</s> arrived in his presence,
the journey made easy by the horse <s>Balāhaka</s>.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> too, upon seeing her, his spirit reviving,
regarded her as <s>Kādambarī</s> herself and touched her again and again.
Then he asked confidently: 'Tell me the story of <s>Kādambarī</s> —

children.text: kim asmākaṃ smaraty eṣā ruṣitehāgamanena kim //
children.translated_text: does she remember us? Or is she angry at our departure?'
She, looking at <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> as if with reproach, said:

children.text: kim etaccintayā deva gurūn ārādhaya sthiram //
children.translated_text: 'Why think about this, O lord? Serve your elders steadfastly.
She has been offered to you by the well-pleased <s>Makaraketana</s> (the god of love) himself,
by fate's decree, as <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune) by the ocean to <s>Śrī's</s> lord (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).
And why have you cast that young girl, tender with fresh affection,
like a young creeper, into the fierce forest fire of separation?
When she learned through <s>Keyūraka</s> of your departure, O lord,
she trembled like a rice-vine struck by a thunderbolt.

children.text: labdhasthairyāvadan māṃ ca pattralekhe kim īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: Having regained her composure, she said to me: "O <s>Pattralekhā</s>, what is this?

children.text: yuktam etasya yanmanye rakṣāṃsy api na kurvate //
children.translated_text: Is this fitting for him? I think even protective charms cannot avail."

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti niḥśvāsair vardhamānair dinair iva /
children.translated_text: From then on, with sighs increasing like the days,
like a summer night overtaken [by the sun], she wasted away slowly, slowly.
Not finding the fragrance of flowers, the bees that formerly came by habit
now avoid her tresses from a distance.
Her eyes, their corners reddened by weeping, their collyrium long forgotten,
have abandoned their sweetness and taken on an astringent hue.
Abandoning the long-standing art of painting leaf-patterns [on her cheeks],
she now makes a new ornament for her cheeks — strings of tear-drop pearls.
Her lower lip, naturally soft and ruddy,

children.text: mlānim ānīyate tasyā niḥśvāsair adharaḥ svaraiḥ //
children.translated_text: is brought to pallor by her sighs, with their unmatched, intensified heat.

children.text: stanau ca virahe tasyāḥ śokān na hi bahiṣkṛtau /
children.translated_text: And in separation, her breasts are not freed from sorrow
by the necklaces, camphor, and sandalwood paste applied as remedies against the burning.
The fire of separation in her [burns on] despite the streams of the essence of her beauty;

children.text: vāḍavaś cābdhinā naiti śamam ity adbhutadvayam //
children.translated_text: and the submarine fire is not quenched by the ocean — both are wondrous.
Now she rolls about distraught by the lake like a <s>haṃsī</s> (female swan),
now in the garden like a doe, now on the sandy bank like a <s>cakravākī</s> bird.
Repeatedly embracing you, imagined before her by her own fancy,

children.text: śūnye bhujalate vīkṣya vilakṣā patati kṣitau //
children.translated_text: seeing her vine-like arms empty, she falls abashed to the ground.

children.text: mā gād ayam upālabdhaḥ saṃkalpād api dūrataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Lest he go away, reproached, far even from imagination" —

children.text: ity upālabhate na tvāṃ bhīteva manasāpi sā //
children.translated_text: thus thinking, she does not reproach you, afraid as it were even in her mind.
Her meditation is filled with your form, her words incline toward your name,
her gaze is fixed upon your body — such is her present state.
How much of her suffering of separation can be described by another?
For it is knowable through one's own experience and is felt by her alone.
Wishing to say something, her lip quivering repeatedly,
she is restrained as if by some weighty presence dwelling in her heart.
Writhing her limbs upon the ground like a female serpent, at one point

children.text: diśo vīkṣya madutsaṅge nidhāya mukham abravīt //
children.translated_text: she, gazing at the quarters, placed her face in my lap and spoke:

children.text: uttiṣṭhānaya taṃ gatvā jīvantīṃ māṃ yadīcchasi /
children.translated_text: "Rise, go and bring him — if you wish me to remain alive.

children.text: ahaṃ gantum aśaktā hi sudūram idam antaram //
children.translated_text: I am unable to traverse this immense distance myself.

children.text: sthitāyāṃ tvayi jīvāmi tvatsparśena yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: While you remain, I live, somehow, through your touch;

children.text: gatāyāṃ tu ciraṃ kālaṃ na sahante mamāsavaḥ //
children.translated_text: but if you go away for long, my life-breaths will not endure."'

children.text: iti śrutvā ca dṛṣṭvā ca samāyātāsmy ataḥ param /
children.translated_text: 'Having thus heard and seen, I have come hereafter;

children.text: devaḥ pramāṇam ity uktvā rudatī virarāma sā //
children.translated_text: the lord is the authority' — having said this, she ceased weeping.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, hearing this, became as if bereft of memory;

children.text: labdhasmṛtiś ciraṃ dadhyau gamane hetum ātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: then, recovering his senses, he pondered long over a reason for his departure.
After some more days had passed, to tell of <s>Kādambarī</s>'s condition,
<s>Keyūraka</s> too arrived swiftly, his mount wearied by the long road.

children.text: sa cojjayinyā vibhavaṃ praviśan vīkṣya vismitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, upon entering and seeing the splendor of <s>Ujjayinī</s>, was amazed

children.text: sthāne nanu mano lagnaṃ svāminyā ity amanyata //
children.translated_text: and thought: 'No wonder my mistress's heart is attached [here].'
Entering, he beheld <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, emaciated in form,
alone like a <s>cakravāka</s> bird, distraught with separation from his beloved,
being fanned by <s>Pattralekhā</s> who stood at his side holding a fly-whisk,
seated on a couch, his body languishing.
Having prostrated himself and seated himself, he was touched firmly on the head
by <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, who inquired after his welfare with affection.
Then, asked by him about news of <s>Kādambarī</s>,
<s>Keyūraka</s>, glancing at <s>Pattralekhā</s>'s face, said this briefly:

children.text: ukto 'si nānayā kiñcid uktaś cet kim iha sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If she has told you nothing — if she has told you, why are you still here?

children.text: uktaś ceha sthitaś cāsi kṛtam āgamanena me //
children.translated_text: If she has told you and you are still here, then my coming is pointless.'

children.text: tathāpi vada saṃdeśam iti tena tu coditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, urged by him, 'Speak the message' —

children.text: punaḥ keyūrakaḥ prāha na hi vijñāpyase mṛṣā //
children.translated_text: <s>Keyūraka</s> again said: "Indeed, you are not being told a falsehood."

children.text: kathaṃ jīvatsu yuṣmāsu viraho hanti mām iti /
children.translated_text: "'How can separation torment me while you are all alive?' —

children.text: tasyāḥ sākūtayā dṛṣṭyā visṛṣṭo 'smi na tadgirā //
children.translated_text: I was dismissed by her meaningful glance, not by those words of hers."
"What need is there of much speaking? Her anguish of separation is such

children.text: adyāpi jīvatīty atra yathā dolāyate manaḥ //
children.translated_text: That even now [my] mind wavers as to whether she is still alive."

children.text: tatkathābhis tathā sthitvā tasminn atha dine ciram /
children.translated_text: Having thus spent that day for a long time with stories about her,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> arranged comfortable quarters for <s>Keyūraka</s>.

children.text: na rākṣaso na cāṇḍālo na kirātaś ca yady aham /
children.translated_text: "If I am neither a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, nor a <s>Kirāta</s>,

children.text: acchodasarasas tīraṃ prāptaṃ māṃ vettha sarvathā //
children.translated_text: Know me as having reached the shore of Lake <s>Acchoda</s> in every way."
Saying "[Return] on the following day," and sending <s>Keyūraka</s> accompanied by <s>Patralekhā</s>,
He sent them off adorned with jewels.

children.text: tayos tu gatayor āsta sutarāṃ khinnamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when those two had gone, he remained with an exceedingly dejected mind,
Seeking with his thoughts some pretext for going [to her].
Then he heard from those appointed that the army camp had arrived,
And had established itself again at a distance of merely two <s>yojanas</s>.

children.text: vaiśampāyanato lapsye kiñcit kāraṇam ity asau /
children.translated_text: "I shall obtain some pretext from <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>" — thus

children.text: pratyudgantum agād enaṃ kaṭakaṃ pitur ājñayā //
children.translated_text: He went to meet the army, by his father's command, to welcome it.
There, seeing the royal camp, announced by <s>Balāhaka</s>,
He asked the general: "Where is <s>Vaiśampāyana's</s> quarters?"

children.text: balāhakas tv adhodṛṣṭir ullikhan medinīṃ muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: But <s>Balāhaka</s>, with downcast eyes, repeatedly scratching the ground,
Said in a choked voice: "<s>Vaiśampāyana</s> is not here."
Then, dismounting from his horse and sitting beneath a tree,
He began to weep, lamenting: "Alas, my friend!"
<s>Balāhaka</s>, falling at the feet of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>,

children.text: deva maivaṃ kṛthāḥ so 'sti jīvann evety avocata //
children.translated_text: Said: "O lord, do not act thus — he is indeed alive!"

children.text: candrāpīḍas tu taṃ prāha naiva śraddhīyate maya /
children.translated_text: But <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> replied to him: "I cannot believe it.

children.text: na vaiśampāyano jīvan muhūrtaṃ māṃ vimuñcati //
children.translated_text: If <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> were alive, he would not leave me even for a moment."

children.text: iti sambhrāntacittaṃ taṃ punar āha balāhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: To him, whose mind was distraught, <s>Balāhaka</s> spoke again:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ deva tadvṛttaṃ yathāsāv iha nāgataḥ //
children.translated_text: "Hear, O lord, the account of why he has not come here."

children.text: deva tādṛśam ādiśya prasthitaṃ tvām anuvrajat /
children.translated_text: "O lord, after you departed giving those instructions, he followed you.
Then, having turned back, he remained right there as before."
"On the following day, having risen and performed the customary rites,
He wandered through the forest clearings to divert himself."
"There, examining each place with signs of recognition,
He seemed to wish to search for something lost, with anxious eyes."
"Then, as the sun was setting, we urged him:

children.text: sthīyatām adya śiṣṭās tu śvo draṣṭāsi vanasthalīḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Stay today; tomorrow you shall see the forest clearings.'"
"But he, still wandering, said as if with indignation:

children.text: yāta yūyaṃ na gantavyaṃ yāvajjīvam ito mayā //
children.translated_text: 'Go, all of you! I shall never leave this place as long as I live.'"

children.text: sa bahūni dināny āsta tatraiva vicaran vane /
children.translated_text: "He remained there for many days, wandering in the forest,

children.text: na ca kenāpyupāyena śaktaś calayituṃ tataḥ //
children.translated_text: And could not be moved from there by any means."
"Even by the entire assembly of kings falling at his feet day and night,
Having practically undertaken a fast unto death, he was entreated yet did not abandon his resolve."

children.text: tatas tatra ciraṃ sthitvā kāryaśeṣam apaśyatā /
children.translated_text: "Then, having stayed there for a long time, seeing no remaining task,

children.text: āyātam iha sainyena tvaṃ pramāṇam ataḥ param //
children.translated_text: We came here with the army. You are now the authority from this point."
Hearing this, fallen into the crisis of grief and amazement,
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s> remained just so, seated at the base of a tree.
Then the king, having learned this news, with ministers and inner court,
Without waiting for the [full] story, came to that very place.

children.text: tatra kṣaṇam iva sthitvā svayaṃ pṛṣṭvā balāhakam /
children.translated_text: Having stayed there for but a moment, having himself questioned <s>Balāhaka</s>,
The king addressed <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, as if reproaching him:
"Surely anger was aroused in him by you, O ill-mannered one,

children.text: yenāntaḥsphuratā so 'dya tvāṃ vihāya vanaṃ śritaḥ //
children.translated_text: Since, with it smoldering within, he has today abandoned you and taken to the forest."

children.text: viyuktau na purā dṛṣṭau yuvāṃ kṣaṇam api kvacit /
children.translated_text: "Never before were you two seen separated even for a moment, anywhere.

children.text: kiṃ jātamadhunā yena tvaṃ gṛhe sa tapovane //
children.translated_text: What has now happened that you are in the house and he in the forest of austerities?"

children.text: vinā na hi nimittena śakyā soḍhuṃ garīyasī /
children.translated_text: "Indeed, without a cause, one cannot endure the very grave
Separation from mother, father, friends, relatives, country, and wealth."

children.text: ity uktavati bhūpāle śukanāsas tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: When the king had thus spoken, thereupon <s>Śukanāsa</s>,
Though his grief was surging within, restraining his agitation, said:
"What is this? Without even investigating, without considering the reality of the matter,
You speak based on mere doubt and conjecture, even though you are wise!"

children.text: alātavṛṣṭir indor vā kṣīrād vā kaṇṭakodgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A shower of fire from the moon, or thorns sprouting from milk —

children.text: tasya manyuḥ kumārād vā kasya sambhāvanāspadam //
children.translated_text: Anger in him toward the prince — who could possibly imagine such a thing?"

children.text: pāpaḥ sa eva durjātaḥ suciraṃ pāṭhitaḥ śukaḥ /
children.translated_text: "That wicked, ill-born parrot who was instructed for so long is the one to blame —
In whom even the nectar of instruction, once sown, has borne fruit like the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison."

children.text: sa tvaṃ kumāra sarvasyāḥ pṛthivyā ekajīvitam /
children.translated_text: "You, O prince, are the sole life of this entire earth.

children.text: durātmano na tasyārthe śokam udvoḍhum arhasi //
children.translated_text: You should not take upon yourself grief for the sake of that wicked one."

children.text: tasmin viratavākye tu patitvā pādayoḥ pituḥ /
children.translated_text: When he had finished speaking, <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, falling at his father's feet,
With tears choking his throat, said with palms joined:
"Father, this is my atonement for the suspected fault.

children.text: gatvā tam ānayāmīha tvam anujñātum arhasi //
children.translated_text: Let me go and bring him here — you should grant permission."
"Seeing him brought here, and questioning him upon oath,

children.text: tato guṇaṃ vā doṣaṃ vā krameṇa mama vetsyasi //
children.translated_text: Then, in due course, you shall ascertain whether it is a virtue or a fault."

children.text: tatrasthaṃ tam anānīya mayaitat svagṛhaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Without bringing him who remains there, I shall not

children.text: na praveṣṭavyam ity eṣa gṛhyatāṃ mama niścayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Enter this house again — let this resolve of mine be accepted."
When he had thus spoken, the king, with eyes filled with tears,

children.text: apaśyan mantriṇo vaktraṃ sa ca tatra bahūktavān //
children.translated_text: Looked at the face of the minister, and the latter spoke at length on the matter.
Though <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> was restrained by his father and by that minister
With every possible means, he did not waver from his resolve.
The charming queen, sprinkling his head with streams of tears

children.text: karuṇaṃ vilapantī ca ciram enam abodhayat //
children.translated_text: And lamenting pitifully, tried for a long time to dissuade him.
"When you are here, I see the little one sitting on my own lap;

children.text: nūnam andhībhavāmy eva tvayi putra gate punaḥ //
children.translated_text: But surely I shall become blind once you depart, O son."

children.text: itthaṃ vilāsavatyā ca tayā ca karuṇoktibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though <s>Vilāsavatī</s> and she softened him for a long time with piteous words,

children.text: ciram ārdrīkṛto 'pyeṣa na jahāti sma niścayam //
children.translated_text: He did not abandon his resolve.
Then, with a voice choked and stammering, its syllables broken by the weight of tears,

children.text: yathā jānāsi putreti katham apy avadan nṛpaḥ //
children.translated_text: The king somehow said: "As you know best, my son."

children.text: dattānujñas tataḥ pitrā praṇamya sakalān gurūn /
children.translated_text: Then, having received permission from his father, bowing to all his elders,
And hearing their blessings, with their streams of tears restrained with effort,

children.text: candrāpīḍaḥ pathi śrāntān vinivartya yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, having gradually turned back the kings who were weary on the road,
Set forth with a light retinue.
"What have I done to him?" — thus the king, his mind burning with grief,

children.text: senayā saha rājāpi viveśa nagarīṃ śanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: Also slowly entered the city with his army.
The general <s>Balāhaka</s>, though urged [to stay] by the king,
Without entering his own house, followed <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>.
<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, going on, eager to see his beloved,
Considered the distance between <s>Kailāsa</s> and the <s>Vindhya</s> as mere straw.

children.text: nājīgaṇad drumān adrīn na nadīr na vanasthalīḥ /
children.translated_text: He took no notice of trees, mountains, rivers, or forest clearings,

children.text: na rātriṃ nāpi divasaṃ dhāvann indrāyudhena saḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor of night, nor of day, riding at full speed on <s>Indrāyudha</s>.
Then the rainy season arrived, full-breasted with swollen clouds,
As if a lovely one, moist with fresh passion, had come forth to meet him.

children.text: tām apy agaṇayitvāsau vrajan katipayair dinaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Disregarding even that, he journeyed on, and within a few days
Reached the shore of Lake <s>Acchoda</s> with its clear waters.
Having unsaddled and changed his garments,

children.text: mahāśvetām atha draṣṭuṃ sa jagāma tadāśramam //
children.translated_text: He then went to the hermitage to see <s>Mahāśvetā</s>.
There he saw <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, ashamed at his sight,
Speaking of her own wickedness, her voice wretched with lamentation.
With eyes whose lashes were motionless in the stupor of not knowing the cause,
When questioned by <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> with his gaze, she spoke:
"Having learned from <s>Keyūraka</s> that you had come by your father's command
And stayed for several days at <s>Kādambarī's</s> abode,"
"Then, returning and sitting here in the hermitage as was proper,
I saw a young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> searching the forest clearings."
*[A <s>yugalaka</s> stanza:]*
"Recognizing me, that one, inclined toward passion,
Intensely distressed me with the impertinence of jesting, suggestive words."
"Though rebuked and though restrained with effort,

children.text: sa bahūni dināny āsta tathā mām upapīḍayan //
children.translated_text: He remained for many days thus tormenting me."

children.text: ekadā tu śayānāṃ mām āgatya niśi nistrapaḥ /
children.translated_text: "One day, shameless, coming to me as I lay sleeping at night,
With palms joined, afflicted by <s>Anaṅga</s> (desire), he begged for the reward of love."
"Then, saying 'Shame!' with anger, drawing water from my water-pot
And invoking the deities, I cursed him thus:"
"'You have been trained only to speak, with the chattering of a parrot.

children.text: gaccha dūraṃ durācāra śuka eva bhaviṣyasi //
children.translated_text: Go far away, O evil-doer — you shall indeed become a parrot!'"

children.text: śāpena tena mahatā madanāgninā vā janmāntaropacitaduṣkṛtakarmaṇā vā /
children.translated_text: "By that great curse, or by the fire of love, or by the evil deeds accumulated in a previous birth,

children.text: citreṇa vā bhagavataś caritena dhātuḥ prāṇān asāv udasṛjan nipapāta corvyām //
children.translated_text: Or by the wondrous play of the Creator — he gave up his life and fell to the ground."

children.text: ākrandataḥ parijanātmaśuco 'paredyur jñāto mayā sa śukanāsasutaḥ sakhā te /
children.translated_text: "The next day, from the cries of his attendants, I learned that he was the son of <s>Śukanāsa</s>, your companion.

children.text: tat paśya māṃ priyavayasyaviyogahetum astatrapām akaruṇāṃ prakhalām abhavyām //
children.translated_text: Therefore, behold me — the cause of your dear friend's separation — shameless, merciless, forward, and abominable!"

children.text: iti śrutvā bhinnaḥ prasabham iva śūlāgraśikhayā kadā tvāṃ paśyeyaṃ kamalamukhi kādambari punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, as if pierced violently by the point of a trident, [he cried:] "When shall I see you again, O lotus-faced <s>Kādambarī</s>?"

children.text: vadann evaṃ śokasphuṭitahṛdayas tatkṣaṇam asūñ jahac candrāpīḍas tarur iva papāta kṣititale //
children.translated_text: Saying thus, his heart shattered by grief, <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> at that very instant gave up his life and fell to the ground like a tree.

children.text: tato bhugnagrīvaṃ mukulitasitāpāṅganayanaṃ prabhāṃ tanvīṃ dīnām iva vidadhataṃ dikṣu śanakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him fallen, with neck bent, white corner-eyes closed, slowly casting a faint, pitiful radiance across the directions,

children.text: kṣitau visrastāṅgaṃ patitam amum ālokya vivaśā mahāśvetā sadyaḥ katham api na yāti sma dalaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: His limbs collapsed upon the earth — beholding this, the helpless <s>Mahāśvetā</s> did not somehow shatter to pieces at once.

children.text: draṣṭuṃ dīnām iva vasumatīm akṣamas tena śūnyāṃ kurvannudyandviradakaruṇākrandinaś cakravākān /
children.translated_text: As if unable to see the earth so pitifully empty, [the sun], making the <s>cakravāka</s> birds raise their mournful elephant-like cries,

children.text: abrahmaṇyadhvanim iva karaurūrdhvaśākhair vimuñcann astaṃ tigmadyutir api tataḥ kṣāmadhāmā jagāma //
children.translated_text: Releasing as it were a sound of sacrilege with upraised branches of rays, even the fierce-rayed sun then set, with diminished luster.

children.text: iti śrīvipaścidvarāgragaṇyācāryaśrībhaṭṭajayantasūnor abhinandasya kṛtau kādambarīkathāsāre ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth canto of the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the revered teacher <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Jayanta</s>, foremost among the supremely learned.
The Seventh Canto.

children.text: tasminn avasare bālā kādambary api vedhasā /
children.translated_text: At that very moment, the young <s>Kādambarī</s> too, by the Creator
Who works the wonder of manifold <s>māyā</s> (illusions), was brought there.

children.text: asau hi pattralekhāyā mukhāt keyūrakasya ca /
children.translated_text: For she, from the mouths of <s>Patralekhā</s> and <s>Keyūraka</s>,
Had without doubt learned that <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> had arrived.
Then, deeming the hermitage of <s>Mahāśvetā</s> to be a fitting place for complete trust,
Free from restraints, she wished to go forth to welcome him who had arrived there.
Fearing that the account of <s>Vaiśampāyana's</s> destruction [would cause]
Anguish in <s>Candrāpīḍa's</s> mind, born of separation from his friend,
<s>Mahāśvetā</s>, recognizing <s>Kādambarī</s> as the means of his consolation,
Was eager for her arrival.

children.text: tasyās taralikāṃ gehaṃ śīghram āgamyatām iti /
children.translated_text: She sent a message to <s>Kādambarī's</s> maid <s>Taralikā</s>, saying: "Come quickly to the house!"

children.text: saṃdiśya prāhiṇot sā ca tūrṇaṃ gatvā tathāvadat //
children.translated_text: And [<s>Taralikā</s>], going swiftly, conveyed the message accordingly.
[A <s>tilaka</s> stanza:]
Emboldened by <s>Mahāśvetā's</s> message, <s>Kādambarī</s> then
Held in her mind the ever-greater eagerness for the important journey.
Accompanied by her bosom friend <s>Madalekhā</s>, who was skilled
In arranging betel, garments, perfumes, and the like,
With <s>Patralekhā</s> leading the way, expert in the conversation of the beloved,

children.text: keyūrakaṃ ca tatraiva dine tāṃ bhuvamāyayau //
children.translated_text: And <s>Keyūraka</s> too, on that very day she arrived at that place.
And as she was coming, a succession of ill omens
Manifested themselves to the young girl, causing her heart to tremble.
She arrived near <s>Mahāśvetā's</s> hermitage when the sun had set
And the lord of the night had risen, its lake of pity heated with anguish.

children.text: āsādya ca tam uddeśaṃ karuṇaṃ rodanadhvanim /
children.translated_text: Approaching that place, she then heard the piteous sound of weeping,
With its echoes issuing from the caverns at the forest's edge.
"I think <s>Mahāśvetā</s> herself has arrived on this path" —

children.text: ity asau śaṅkamāneva viveśa drutam āśramam //
children.translated_text: Thus suspecting, she quickly entered the hermitage.
Then, entering, she saw her lord of life lying thus,

children.text: mahāśvetāṃ ca tām ārtaninādaṃ rudatīṃ bhṛśam //
children.translated_text: And <s>Mahāśvetā</s> weeping bitterly with wretched cries.
Gazing at <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, bewildered and overwhelmed by blossoming grief,
Beating her chest violently, weeping, she fell into a swoon.
<s>Pattralekhā</s> too, gazing at the form of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> [lying there],
suddenly lost consciousness, falling upon the stone surface.

children.text: kādambaryā tu dhairyeṇa pṛṣṭā taralikā tadā /
children.translated_text: When <s>Taralikā</s> was then asked by <s>Kādambarī</s> with composure,
she narrated everything — the entire sequence of his death, as it had occurred.
Hearing that, abandoning the distress natural to women,
she spoke to <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, who had regained consciousness, and to <s>Madalekhā</s>:
"I am exhausted now by this heavy weeping,
which has been flowing in thick, continuous streams for so long."

children.text: yathāyogyena gacchāmi na hi śaknomi roditum /
children.translated_text: "I shall depart in the fitting manner — for I cannot weep anymore;

children.text: sakhi me darśitaḥ panthā nāthenaiva mahātmanā //
children.translated_text: O friend, the path has been shown to me by the noble lord himself."
"He who neither wept nor lamented at the separation from a dear friend,

children.text: prāṇāneva priyānaujjhītsa panthāḥ kva gato mama //
children.translated_text: but gave up his beloved life-breaths — where has that path gone from me?"

children.text: yuktaṃ sakhi mahāśvete tava prāṇitum īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: "It is fitting, O friend <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, that you continue to live thus;
you have been kept alive by the gods, with the hope of reunion with him again."
"But I, whose desires have been shattered by fate in every way,
what shall I do with these wretched life-breaths, excluded from all good fortune?"

children.text: madalekhe tathā kuryās tāto 'mbā ca kule sthitau /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Madalekhā</s>, act in such a way — my father and mother stand in the family —
that they do not abandon their composure through the torment of separation from me."
"And you yourself must dwell in my residence
so that spiders do not rest in the jeweled windows."

children.text: kumāras tatra citrastho mayaiva likhitaḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: "The prince depicted in a painting there, drawn by me with my own hand —

children.text: rakṣaṇīyo yathā nāstam eti citrasthito 'py asau //
children.translated_text: he must be protected so that even the painted one does not perish."
"The painting of <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of love), set upon the gem-wall at the head of the bed,
though worshipped in vain, should be placed somewhere [safe]."
"The pleasure-hill should be given to a peaceful ascetic;

children.text: tatroṣitaṃ kumāreṇa na hi so 'nyasya śobhate //
children.translated_text: since the prince dwelt there, it is not fitting for anyone else."
"In the midst of my garden-lake, adorned with a grove of lotuses,
there dwells a flock of royal swans that have made their home."
"And nearby is a pleasure-pool filled by water-fountains;

children.text: snehān mayā svayaṃ siktam asti līlāvanaṃ navam //
children.translated_text: there is a new pleasure-garden that I myself planted with affection."
"In it, I married a <s>mālatī</s> jasmine to a <s>bakula</s> tree;

children.text: muktaḥ kaṅkaṇako nāsyā mocanīyas tvayaiva saḥ //
children.translated_text: I released the bracelet [for the ceremony] — you alone must unfasten it [for her]."
"And that young <s>aśoka</s> tree-sapling was adopted as my child;
it must be nourished with water poured from your own hands, like mother's milk."

children.text: gṛhe muhur apaśyantī mām asau capalekṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: "And that restless-eyed doe in my house, not seeing me repeatedly,

children.text: nūnaṃ hariṇikā cāste prāpayes tāṃ ca kānanam //
children.translated_text: must surely be distressed — send her also to the forest."

children.text: śukaḥ sa parihāso me kālinī sā ca śārikā /
children.translated_text: "That parrot is my jester, and that mynah bird <s>Kālinī</s> —

children.text: yathā na kalahāyete tathā kuryāḥ pratikṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: see to it at every moment that they do not quarrel."
"The female mongoose, always fondled in my lap,

children.text: svāṅke śāyayitavyāsau yathā yāti na dūrataḥ //
children.translated_text: should be made to sleep in your own lap, so that she does not wander far."

children.text: kiṃ kāryam athavā gehe cintayā dīrghayānayā /
children.translated_text: "Or what use is this protracted anxiety about the household?
Prepare the funeral pyre quickly, with blazing fire!"

children.text: keyūraka ciraṃ kiṃ mām atidīnām avekṣase /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Keyūraka</s>, why do you gaze at me, so utterly wretched, for so long?
Rise, gather firewood, assemble the fire!"
"But how can this body, an ocean of gracefulness, be consigned to fire?

children.text: kumāram amum ādāya patāmi varam ambhasi //
children.translated_text: Better that I plunge into the water, taking the prince with me."
"When the prince gave up his life in an instant through grief for a friend,

children.text: iyantam api jīvantī kālaṃ lajje 'ham ātmanā //
children.translated_text: I am ashamed of myself for having lived even this long."

children.text: draṣṭavyāsi kadety evam abhidhāyaiva māṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: "'When shall I see you?' — saying just this to me, he departed;
he would now say, 'She is taking too long.'"
Thus, seeing <s>Kādambarī</s>, now resolved upon immediate death,
the cool-rayed moon seemed to tremble.
It was as if flooded by the waves of the milk-ocean,
and the entire company of maidens, their teeth chattering, [trembled].
Then some person of divine form, standing in the sky,
spoke in a voice as deep and steady as rumbling thunder-clouds:

children.text: tvaṃ hi vatse mahāśvete pūrvamāśvāsitā mayā /
children.translated_text: "O child <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, you were consoled by me before;
your beloved <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> still abides near me even now."
"And this <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, as if sleeping for a short while,
let him remain here with his beauty undiminished — the beloved of <s>Kādambarī</s>."
"For by him, having regained imperishable, enduring life,
the joy of a tight embrace will be given to <s>Kādambarī</s>."
"Let this firm conviction be in the hearts of you both:

children.text: na sprakṣyati vikāro yad enaṃ bhūtasvabhāvajaḥ //
children.translated_text: that no change born of the nature of elements shall touch him."

children.text: ity uktvā jyotiṣā tena sahasaiva tirodadhe /
children.translated_text: Having said this, that celestial being suddenly vanished;
and the entire company of maidens was filled with wonder.

children.text: pattralekhā ca tenaiva jyotiṣo vacanena sā /
children.translated_text: <s>Pattralekhā</s> too, by the words of that same celestial being,

children.text: labdhasaṃjñā samutthāya gatvā ca tvaritaiḥ padaiḥ //
children.translated_text: having regained consciousness, rose and went with hurried steps.
Taking that horse named <s>Indrāyudha</s> by the mane,
together with him, she entered the deep middle of the waters.
<s>Taralikā</s>, as if alarmed, followed her who rushed swiftly,
and she saw <s>Kapiñjala</s> emerging from the midst of the waters.
Reaching out, she described the marvel as she had seen it,
and the wonder of those maidens grew all the more.
Then, bearing thin matted locks, rough with clinging drops of water,
clad in water-soaked bark garments, <s>Kapiñjala</s> was seen by them.
He himself approached and spoke to <s>Mahāśvetā</s>:
"O princess, is not this person even recognized?"

children.text: ahaṃ kapiñjalas tasya vayasyo dayitasya te /
children.translated_text: "I am <s>Kapiñjala</s>, the friend of that beloved of yours;
I deserve to be reproached by you for the wickedness of my long absence."

children.text: kādambaryā tvayā caitāḥ śrutāś candramaso giraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Both you, <s>Kādambarī</s>, and you have heard the words of the moon;

children.text: madīyam api vṛttāntam adhunā śṛṇutaṃ yuvām //
children.translated_text: now hear from me my own story as well."

children.text: apy utkṣipya tathā nīte vayasye tena tatkṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: "When my friend was snatched up and carried away by him at that very moment,

children.text: ahaṃ gaganam utplutya tam evānusarann agām //
children.translated_text: I, leaping into the sky, went following him."
"Then he, having leaped far away and entered the orb of the moon,

children.text: paścād eva praviṣṭaṃ mām avalokyedam abravīt //
children.translated_text: saw me who had entered after him, and spoke thus:"

children.text: kapiñjala mṛgāṅkaṃ māṃ viddhi so 'haṃ tavāmunā /
children.translated_text: "'O <s>Kapiñjala</s>, know me to be the Moon. I am he — by this
friend of yours I was cursed in vain, while you were at <s>Hemakūṭa</s>.'"
"'For the course of the world must be borne by me as a guardian of the worlds;

children.text: udito 'haṃ nije kāle tataḥ pravikiran karān //
children.translated_text: I rose at my appointed time, spreading my rays.'"
"'This one, his passion increased by the touch of my rays,
with his life-breath at the edge of his throat, cursed me harshly:'"
"'Just as I, tormented by separation, have today been destroyed by you coming,
so shall you too die, O Moon, birth after birth.'"

children.text: pratiśapto mayāpyeṣa tvam apy evaṃ mariṣyasi /
children.translated_text: "'And I cursed him in return: You too shall die just so,
like me — [I spoke thus,] with anger aroused by the pain of the innocent one's curse.'"
"'Then my anger gradually diminished, seeing that
he was a son-in-law through his connection with <s>Mahāśvetā</s>.'"
"'The great ascetic <s>Śvetaketu</s> might devise a remedy;
I shall protect his body with my nectar-filled rays.'"

children.text: ity utkṣipya mayehāyam ānītas tvaṃ ca satvaram /
children.translated_text: "'Thus, having lifted him, I brought him here; and you, quickly
go and report this account to <s>Śvetaketu</s>.'"
"Having heard the Moon's words, I, flying up to the sky,
in my swift course, inadvertently overstepped some aerial being."

children.text: sa ca mām aśapat kopād aśveneva tapobalāt /
children.translated_text: "And he cursed me in anger, through the power of his austerities like a horse:

children.text: tvayāhaṃ laṅghitas tasmād aśva eva bhaviṣyasi //
children.translated_text: 'Since you have overstepped me, you shall become a horse!'"
"I, bowing to him, said: 'With a mind blinded by grief for a friend,

children.text: pramādān na tapodarpān mama tat saṃhara krudham //
children.translated_text: through inadvertence, not through the pride of austerity — withdraw your anger.'"

children.text: sa tv abhāṣata datto 'yaṃ śāpo bhavati nānyathā /
children.translated_text: "But he spoke: 'This curse is given and cannot be otherwise.'
'The Moon shall assume sonship of the king <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>, who is performing austerities in <s>Ujjayinī</s> for a son, with visible proof;'
'and <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> [shall become the son] of <s>Śukanāsa</s>, his minister.'
"'You shall serve as the mount of this son of <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>, the Moon [incarnate];
at the end of that [service], having bathed, the end of the curse shall come.'"
"Hearing that, I fell into the ocean, stunned by the curse;
then, having become a horse, I arose — not born of a womb."

children.text: smṛtis turagabhāve 'pi na me naṣṭā kadācana /
children.translated_text: "Even in horse-form, my memory was never lost;
I was brought here, following the traces of the <s>Kinnaras</s>."

children.text: vīpsānvitaś ca śāpo 'yaṃ parasparam abhūt tayoḥ /
children.translated_text: "And this curse was mutual between those two, involving repetition;
therefore, their [fate] must assuredly [unfold] through a second birth."
"So I shall go to tell <s>Śvetaketu</s> the account as it happened,
and to learn where those two shall take their second birth."
From <s>Kapiñjala</s>'s story, recognizing <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>
in the form of <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, <s>Mahāśvetā</s> was overcome with anguish.

children.text: dvitīye 'py aham evāsya jātā janmani mṛtyave /
children.translated_text: "In his second birth too, I alone have become the cause of his death;
he was cursed because of his love for me" — thus she lamented.

children.text: kapiñjalas tadā tv evaṃ rudatīṃ tām avārayat /
children.translated_text: <s>Kapiñjala</s> then restrained her who was weeping thus,

children.text: abravīc cāvadhiḥ pūrṇaḥ prāyo duḥkhasya vartate //
children.translated_text: and said: "The limit of suffering is most likely already at hand."
"In but a short time, you will again place in <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>'s
lotus-like palm the prayer-bead rosary, with a smile."
"And <s>Kādambarī</s> too shall be gladdened
by <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>'s rich words, adorned with nectar of sweet, charming smiles."

children.text: kādambarī tam aprākṣīd bhagavan sā kva vartate /
children.translated_text: <s>Kādambarī</s> asked him: "O venerable one, where does she —

children.text: pattralekheti sa tv āha mayā nājñāyi tadgatiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Pattralekhā</s> — dwell?" He replied: "Her whereabouts are unknown to me."
Having said this, <s>Kapiñjala</s> flew up to the sky,
scattering drops of water from his pores, indistinguishable from drops of <s>Acchoda</s> lake.
After his departure, <s>Mahāśvetā</s> and <s>Kādambarī</s>, in that same manner,
spent the night with that story, trembling with grief and wonder.
In the account of <s>Mahāśvetā</s>'s story, with even firmer conviction,

children.text: kādambaryāḥ sthiraṃ citte sā pratyayam ajījanat //
children.translated_text: <s>Kādambarī</s>'s heart gave birth to steadfast faith.
On the following day, having raised [his body] upon a spacious crystal slab,
delightful, rough with grains of camphor-frost,

children.text: abhiṣicya jalaiḥ svacchair anulipya ca candanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: having anointed [him] with clear waters and applied sandalwood paste,
<s>Kādambarī</s> worshipped the body of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> for a long time.

children.text: yadi satyo 'yam āśvāsaḥ sarvaṃ svastham athānyathā /
children.translated_text: "If this consolation is true, then all is well; otherwise,

children.text: kva gato me tadā mṛtyur ity antar niścikāya sā //
children.translated_text: where then is death gone from me?" — thus she resolved within.

children.text: jagāda ca mahāśvetām idānīṃ nanu na trape /
children.translated_text: And she said to <s>Mahāśvetā</s>: "Now surely I am not ashamed
to address you as 'friend,' you who share the same austerity of suffering as I."
"Fate, having ordained an equality of joy and sorrow for us both,
has not tainted our long-established friendship."

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti sā mūrtim arcayantyāsta tāpasī /
children.translated_text: From then on, that ascetic woman worshipped the form
of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> day and night, as if [worshipping] the crescent-crowned <s>Śiva</s>.
As the days passed, seeing the unchanging condition

children.text: candrāpīḍasya paśyantī sthirām āśāṃ babandha sā //
children.translated_text: of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>'s body, she bound herself to firm hope.
Then, summoning the general, she spoke to <s>Balāhaka</s>:
"The entire account, full of many wonders, is known to you."
"And our conviction has arisen from the non-decay of his body's radiance;
you should go to <s>Ujjayinī</s> for the sake of consoling our lord [the king]."

children.text: so 'bravīd devi tatrānyaṃ prajñātaṃ prahiṇomy aham /
children.translated_text: He replied: "O lady, I shall send another trusted person there;

children.text: yuvarājam ihotsṛjya na gantuṃ svayam utsahe //
children.translated_text: I do not have the heart to go myself, leaving the crown prince here."
Then a man named <s>Tvaritaka</s>, a close servant of the king,
was sent by him, along with a letter in his own handwriting.

children.text: sa gatvojjayinīṃ prāpya sarvaṃ rājñe nyavedayat /
children.translated_text: He, having gone and reached <s>Ujjayinī</s>, reported everything to the king;
the king, together with the inner court and ministers, heard it all in order.
Then, with his consciousness bewildered by hearing of his son's heart-stopping [death],
he did not firmly believe in the latter part of the account.
<s>Śukanāsa</s>, however, said to him: "For one who knows the variety of <s>karma</s>,
who has heard the ancient lore and treatises, O lord, what confusion is there in this?"
"The assumption of mortal bodies by gods and sages

children.text: śrūyate hi purāṇeṣu smṛtāv api ca paṭhyate //
children.translated_text: is heard of in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and is also recounted in the <s>Smṛtis</s>."
"The wondrous excellences of men, befitting superhuman beings,

children.text: kim apy alaukikaṃ bījam anumāpayituṃ kṣamāḥ //
children.translated_text: are capable of suggesting some extraordinary origin."

children.text: kumāraś ca guṇair indor atidūraṃ na bhidyate /
children.translated_text: "And the prince is not far removed from the Moon in his qualities;

children.text: sā kāntir ākṛtiḥ śaktiḥ kva dṛṣṭā cānyamānuṣe //
children.translated_text: that radiance, that form, that power — where else has it been seen in any [mere] human?"

children.text: svapne devīmukhe dṛṣṭaś candramās tu viśaṃs tvayā /
children.translated_text: 'The moon seen by you in a dream entering the queen's face,
and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman bearing the white lotus mark seen by me —

children.text: śāpa eva tayor āsīd āvayos tu paro varaḥ /
children.translated_text: for those two [beings] it was indeed a curse; but for us it was a supreme boon,
that deities attain the state of sons in the houses of mortals.
Moreover, how could <s>Kapiñjala</s>, with his unimpeded movement in the sky,

children.text: ācakṣīta kathaṃ mithyā turago nu kva tādṛśaḥ //
children.translated_text: speak falsely? And where else [could one find] such a horse [as his]?

children.text: idaṃ kvānyatra dṛṣṭaṃ vā jīvitenojjhito 'pi yaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where else has this been seen — that one who has been abandoned by life,

children.text: pañcabhūtātmako dehaḥ sa yad eti na vikriyām //
children.translated_text: whose body is made of the five elements, does not undergo decay?
Would <s>Tvaritaka</s> speak falsely? Would <s>Balāhaka</s> write falsely?
This suspicion is not fitting for you, who have well-tested servants.'
'Before long, you shall behold the prince, freed from the torment of the curse,

children.text: śaśinam iva vidhuntudena muktaṃ vyapagataśāpakadarthanaṃ kumāram //
children.translated_text: causing the world to overflow with joy, like the moon released by <s>Rāhu</s>.'
Even as the king heard the minister's words, his heart, made unsteady by love for his son,

children.text: na dhṛtiṃ pratipadyate sma ceto gamane ca vyavasāyam ālalambe //
children.translated_text: did not attain composure, and his mind inclined toward resolve to depart.
Then, together with his queens whose eyes were filled with tears, accompanied by his own minister, the king went to the bank of the <s>Acchodā</s> river;

children.text: śithilitasakalāsthaḥ pārthivas taṃ ca yāntaṃ janapadapuralokaḥ sarva evānvagacchat //
children.translated_text: the king, all his strength loosened, and the people of the towns and countryside — everyone followed him as he went.

children.text: tasmin gate 'tha vijanāpaṇavīthikāntā kāntārabhūr iva tadojjayinī babhūva /
children.translated_text: When he had departed, <s>Ujjayinī</s>, with its market streets and lanes deserted, became like a wilderness,

children.text: yāte divaṃ sakalalokamanobhirāme rāme yathā hatasamṛddhir abhūd ayodhyā //
children.translated_text: just as <s>Ayodhyā</s> became bereft of prosperity when <s>Rāma</s>, the delight of all minds, departed for heaven.

children.text: gatvā nṛpaḥ sutam avekṣya ciraṃ ruditvā tat tad vilapya saha tatra vilāsavatyā /
children.translated_text: Having gone, the king gazed upon his son, wept for a long time, and lamented this and that with <s>Vilāsavatī</s> there;

children.text: utsṛjya rājyavibhavaṃ yativad vyadhatta tatraiva valkaladharaḥ sthitim adya tāvat //
children.translated_text: then, renouncing the splendor of his kingdom, he lived like an ascetic, wearing bark-cloth, right there from that day forward.

children.text: ity uktvā kṛtajṛmbhikaḥ kṣaṇam iva sthitvācacakṣe punar jābalir bhagavān aho bata rasād dīrghā kathā varṇitā /
children.translated_text: 'Thus spoke the blessed <s>Jābāli</s>, pausing for a moment with a yawn, and then said again: "Ah, what a long story has been narrated with delight!

children.text: tadyo 'sau śukanāsasūnur anayā śapto mahāśvetayā vaiśampāyana eṣa so 'dya śukatāṃ tenāgataḥ karmaṇā //
children.translated_text: He who was the son of <s>Śukanāsa</s>, cursed by <s>Mahāśvetā</s> — that <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> has now, by that deed, attained the state of a parrot."'

children.text: api cāvinayena kopitaḥ śukanāso 'sya pitā yad abravīt /
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, his father <s>Śukanāsa</s>, angered by his improper conduct, had said:

children.text: śuka eva vṛthā sa pāṭhitaḥ phalitaṃ tac ca vaco 'dya śāpavat //
