children.translated_text: "A parrot indeed he is, uselessly taught!" — and that word too has borne fruit today, like a curse.'

children.text: śrutvaitāṃ tu kathāṃ tapodhanagaṇaiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ punar vismitaiḥ ko hetur bhagavan yad asya madanas tāvān muner apy abhūt /
children.translated_text: 'Hearing this story, the hosts of ascetics, amazed, asked again: "What is the reason, O blessed one, that the sage too experienced such a great passion?"

children.text: jābāliḥ punar āha nanv abhihitaṃ strīvīryataḥ kevalād utpanno 'yam ato rajasvalatayā nārīsvabhāvo 'bhavat //
children.translated_text: <s>Jābāli</s> replied: "Has it not been told? He was born solely from the power of a woman; therefore, due to being born of female essence, he had a woman's nature."'

children.text: viratavacasi tasminn etad uktvā maharṣau rajanir api samāptiṃ sā kathāvat prapede /
children.translated_text: 'When that great sage had ceased speaking, having said this, the night too reached its end, like the story;
thereafter, the assembly of sages attained success in their meditation practices appropriate for the morning twilight juncture.'

children.text: iti śrīvipaścidvarāgragaṇyācāryaśrībhaṭṭajayantasūnor abhinandasya kṛtau kādambarīkathāsāre saptamaḥ sargaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh canto of the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the teacher, the venerable <s>Śrī Bhaṭṭa Jayanta</s>, foremost among the assembly of the most distinguished scholars.
Eighth Canto
'Then, upon me, who had heard the complete sequence of the story told by <s>Jābāli</s>,
the memory of my former birth's deeds touched me, even in my infant state as a bird.
Having been the son of <s>Śvetaketu</s>, I became the son of <s>Śukanāsa</s>;
that <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> — I am he today, born as the son of a bird.
With the memory of my births aroused, my speech became eloquent,
and the sciences of former births spontaneously entered my heart.

children.text: yathaiva cānye saṃskārāḥ prāktanā mām upāgaman /
children.translated_text: And just as other impressions from former lives came to me,
so too did my love for <s>Mahāśvetā</s> come in the same way.
Then, nurtured with increasing affection by <s>Hārīta</s>, gradually,
having grown wings, I attained the ability to traverse the sky.
As days passed, slowly maturing in youth,
I wished to go to <s>Mahāśvetā</s>'s hermitage, eager to see her.

children.text: acintayaṃ ca janmedaṃ vihagasyāpi yātu me /
children.translated_text: And I thought: "Let even this life as a bird pass for me
sleeping in a tree-hollow near <s>Mahāśvetā</s>'s hermitage."

children.text: ekadā tv atha jābāler āśramaṃ samupāgamat /
children.translated_text: One day, however, <s>Kapiñjala</s> came to <s>Jābāli</s>'s hermitage,
at his father's command, bound by his friendship and affection.

children.text: sa ca papraccha hārītaṃ kva vaiśampāyanaḥ śukaḥ /
children.translated_text: He asked <s>Hārīta</s>: "Where is the parrot <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>?"
Having gained recognition, I said: "I am he."

children.text: tataś ciram arodīt sa svavakṣasi nidhāya mām /
children.translated_text: Then he wept for a long time, holding me to his chest:
"Alas, what a state has befallen my friend <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>!"
I too, weeping, said to him: "Why do you weep, O <s>Kapiñjala</s>?

children.text: tvayāpi matkṛte dṛṣṭā sakhe kaṣṭatarā daśā //
children.translated_text: You yourself, my friend, have seen an even more terrible fate on my account.

children.text: kva heṣā kva japābhyāsaḥ kva paryāṇaṃ kva valkalam /
children.translated_text: Where now is the neighing, and where the chanting of prayers? Where the saddle, and where the bark-cloth?

children.text: kvopavītaṃ kva vā valgā kva muniḥ kva turaṅgamaḥ //
children.translated_text: Where the sacred thread, and where the reins? Where the sage, and where the horse?"

children.text: tataḥ kṣaṇam iva sthitvā tātasaṃdeśam abravīt /
children.translated_text: Then, staying just a moment, <s>Kapiñjala</s> delivered his father's message,
briefly, being in haste to depart again:

children.text: tātas tvām ādideśaivaṃ vatsa doṣas tavātra kaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your father has instructed you thus: 'My child, what fault is yours in this?
The modifications of <s>rajas</s> (passion) are natural for those born purely of a woman's seed.

children.text: alpāyuṣaṃ viditvāpi jāte tvayi na yan mayā /
children.translated_text: Though I knew you to be short-lived, that I did not take countermeasures

children.text: kṛtā pratikriyā tatra tadālasyaṃ hi māmakam //
children.translated_text: when you were born — that was indeed my own negligence.
But now a sacrifice for longevity has been undertaken; until it is completed,

children.text: na yāvad bhavatā tāvan na gantavyam itaḥ kvacit //
children.translated_text: you must not go anywhere from here.

children.text: ahaṃ tvadantike sthātum icchann api nivāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though I wish to stay near you, I have been prevented
by your father, being assigned to a portion of the ritual duties there.'"
Having told me this, embracing me, and with the obligation to return to the rites,

children.text: krameṇāmantrya sa munīn pratasthe divam utpatan //
children.translated_text: having taken leave of the sages in due order, he departed, flying upward to the sky.
Though I had received my father's instruction, as time passed, I was forcibly
brought under the sway of <s>Kāma</s> (Love), whose [other] side is obstruction.
Having endured for a long time there the wondrous terrors of love,
I formed the intention to depart, transgressing the command of my elder.

children.text: ekadā tv āśramaṃ śūnyaṃ vīkṣya nirgatatāpasam /
children.translated_text: One day, seeing the hermitage empty, the ascetics having gone out,
alone, I suddenly took flight and set off toward the northern direction.
Having flown not far, unpracticed in traversing long distances,

children.text: krāntas tṛṣā ca klāntyā ca jalaṃ kvacid atarkayam //
children.translated_text: I was overcome by thirst and fatigue, and I searched somewhere for water.

children.text: tataḥ kvāpi payaḥ pītvā kiñcid ādaśya cañcunā /
children.translated_text: Then, having drunk water somewhere and pecked a little with my beak,
weary, I entered the hollow of some tree to rest.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ tatra niṣaṇṇasya tadā me nidrayā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having sat there for just a moment, my mind and body
were seized by deep sleep, as if by chains and fetters.
Then, waking from sleep, I saw before me, not far away,
a young <s>Mātaṅga</s> (outcaste) man, looking satisfied as if from capturing me.
Inferring from his appearance and actions his desire for my flesh,
I spoke some words, soft with entreaty, for the purpose of freeing myself:

children.text: bhadra saumyākṛtis tvaṃ hi na māṃsārthīva dṛśyase /
children.translated_text: "Good sir, you are gentle in appearance and do not seem to be one who seeks flesh;
for it is not fitting for a flesh-seeker to wait for the breaking of sleep.

children.text: tad unmuñcatu māṃ bhadraḥ sukhaṃ yāmi yathepsitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore let the good sir release me; I shall go happily as I please.

children.text: mayā baddhena ko 'rthas te kā vimuktena vā kṣatiḥ //
children.translated_text: What use am I to you, bound? And what loss to you if released?"

children.text: so 'bravīn na svatantreṇa gṛhīto 'si mayā śuka /
children.translated_text: He replied: "You have not been caught by me of my own volition, O parrot;

children.text: prathitas tvaṃ hi jālāber āśrame suciraṃ sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: for you are famous, having long dwelt in <s>Jābāli</s>'s hermitage.

children.text: sa tvaṃ gato mama svāmiduhituḥ karṇagocaram /
children.translated_text: You have come to the ears of my master's daughter;
having been caught by her command, how can I release you?"

children.text: punar ākhyām amuṃ saumya yuvāsi smaravedanām /
children.translated_text: "I say again, O gentle one — you are young, you know the pain of love;

children.text: jānāsi na priyotkaṇṭhākṛṣṭaṃ māṃ roddhum arhasi //
children.translated_text: you should not confine me, who am drawn by longing for my beloved."
He said: "A servant, even a young one, must not transgress

children.text: svāmino 'laṅghanīyaṃ tat kathaṃ tvāṃ tyaktum utsahe //
children.translated_text: the command of his master; how then could I bring myself to release you?"

children.text: avocaṃ punar apy enaṃ śāpāj jātismaro muniḥ /
children.translated_text: I said to him again: "I am a sage who remembers his former births, cursed into parrot-form;

children.text: śukībhūto 'smi māṃ muñca paraṃ puṇyam avāpsyasi //
children.translated_text: release me — you will obtain great merit."

children.text: sa tvāha nāhaṃ jānāmi muniṃ gandharvameva vā /
children.translated_text: But he said: "I do not know whether you are a sage, a <s>Gandharva</s>,

children.text: rākṣasaṃ vā piśācaṃ vā nīta evāsi pakvaṇam //
children.translated_text: a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon), or a <s>Piśāca</s> (goblin) — you are being taken to the settlement, that's all."

children.text: ity uktvādāya pāṇau mām anaiṣīt pakvaṇaṃ balāt /
children.translated_text: Saying this, taking me in his hand, he carried me forcibly to the settlement
and made me enter the foul dwelling of the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> maiden.
Seeing it — slippery with fresh cow-flesh, fat, and blood-mud,
teeming with crawling worms — it was as if my wretched life-breaths departed.

children.text: atha mātaṅgakanyāyai sa mām asyai nyavedayat /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Mātaṅga</s> man presented me to the maiden, [saying:]

children.text: svāminy ayam ihānītaḥ sa vaiśampāyanaḥ śukaḥ //
children.translated_text: "My mistress, this is that parrot <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, brought here."

children.text: sākūtam iva māṃ vīkṣya snehabāṣpārdrayā dṛśā /
children.translated_text: Looking at me as if with hidden purpose, with eyes moist with tears of affection,
holding me to her breast for a moment, she placed me in a closed cage.

children.text: tato 'timahatā cakre śokena hṛdi me padam /
children.translated_text: Then, immense sorrow made its place in my heart:

children.text: munir bhūtvādya caṇḍālyā ahaṃ krīḍāśukaḥ sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Having been a sage, today I am a pet parrot of a <s>Caṇḍālī</s>!

children.text: vyaktāṃ vidadhatā vācaṃ jātiṃ smarayatā nijām /
children.translated_text: By giving me articulate speech and making me remember my own birth,
alas, <s>Jābāli</s>, with his divine sight, has done me a disservice!

children.text: aho bata mahat kaṣṭam aviṣahyam upasthitam /
children.translated_text: Alas, what a great, unbearable calamity has befallen me —
I, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, must spend my time in a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>'s dwelling!
So be it — by fasting alone I shall abandon this wretched life;

children.text: tāḍyamāno 'pi nāśnāmi na vācaṃ visṛjāmi ca //
children.translated_text: even if beaten, I shall not eat, nor shall I utter a word."

children.text: evamudvejitaiṣā māṃ hanyādvā yadi vā tyajet /
children.translated_text: "Thus provoked, she will either kill me or release me;

children.text: bhavaty ubhayathāpy eṣa panthāḥ śreyaskaro mama //
children.translated_text: in either case, this path is beneficial for me."
As I had thus formed my resolve, this <s>Caṇḍāla</s> maiden,

children.text: eṣā caṇḍālakanyā mām ākhyan madhurayā girā //
children.translated_text: having brought fruits and water, addressed me in sweet words:

children.text: phalāny aśāna pānīyam upayuṅkṣva kim īkṣase /
children.translated_text: "Eat these fruits, drink the water — why do you stare so?
Even with your vow of silence broken today, why do you cling to silence?

children.text: munir jātismaro 'si tvaṃ yadi ko 'pi tathāpi te /
children.translated_text: Even if you are some sage who remembers former births,
still, today the mode of life appropriate to an animal birth is what is approved for you.

children.text: na tiryagadhikāraṃ hi śāstraṃ śāstravido viduḥ /
children.translated_text: For those who know the scriptures know that the scriptures do not apply to animals;
and where indeed are sacraments like the tonsure and investiture for animals?
And if you now wish to observe distinctions of edible and inedible,

children.text: tat kim ucchiṣṭaśaucādi nāśrame 'py āśritaṃ tvayā //
children.translated_text: then why did you not also observe purity rules regarding leftovers in the hermitage?

children.text: āpatkāle dvijātīnām apy anāśyaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Even for the twice-born, in times of distress, there is nothing that may not be eaten;
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> accepted from our hands the haunch of a dog.
Having fasted for two days, you appear as if wishing to die, my child;

children.text: lakṣyase vatsa mā maivaṃ kṛthā bhuṅkṣva phalodakam //
children.translated_text: do not do this — eat the fruits and water."
Astonished at her words, unlike a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>'s, unfitting for a common woman,
I reflected for a long time thus:

children.text: nūnam eṣā na caṇḍālī madvat kenāpi karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: "Surely she is no <s>Caṇḍālī</s>; like me, through some deed,

children.text: manye gatim imāṃ prāptā madarthenaiva vā punaḥ //
children.translated_text: I think she has attained this condition — or perhaps for my sake alone.

children.text: bibharty urasi māteva paśyati snigdhayā dṛśā /
children.translated_text: She holds me to her breast like a mother, looks at me with affectionate eyes,

children.text: vakti caivam ato 'muṣyāḥ karomi vacanaṃ varam //
children.translated_text: and speaks thus — therefore it is better that I comply with her words."
Thinking thus, I uttered speech and became willing to eat;

children.text: abhojayac ca mām eṣā jananīva dine dine //
children.translated_text: and she fed me day after day, like a mother.

children.text: tattvam asyāḥ parijñātum anvahaṃ prārthanāṃ vyadhām /
children.translated_text: I made daily entreaties to learn her true identity,

children.text: na tv eṣā prārthyamānāpi nijaṃ rūpam adīdṛśat //
children.translated_text: but even when entreated, she did not reveal her true form.

children.text: nityam āśaṅkamāno 'ham etāṃ kām api devatām /
children.translated_text: Always suspecting her to be some deity,
nourished by her, I passed time there in the settlement.
And one day, at the end of the night, I was released from sleep
and saw the entire settlement filled with mostly respectable people.
And [I saw] myself adorned with a fresh, generous golden cage,

children.text: kanyakām īdṛśīṃ caitāṃ dṛṣṭā devena yādṛśī //
children.translated_text: and this maiden appearing as the lord has [just] seen her.'
*couplet*

children.text: tat ko 'haṃ kim ahaṃ tatra rakṣitaś ciram enayā /
children.translated_text: 'Then — who am I? Why was I guarded there for so long by her?

children.text: kasya hetor ihānīta iti rājan na vedmy aham //
children.translated_text: For what reason was I brought here? — this, O king, I do not know.'
Having heard this story narrated by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>,

children.text: sa rājā śūdrakaḥ śayyāgṛhād aṅganam āgamat //
children.translated_text: that King <s>Śūdraka</s> came out from the bedchamber to the courtyard.

children.text: sasambhramaṃ ca nirgatya tūrṇam ānāyayat punaḥ /
children.translated_text: And going out hastily with alarm, he had brought again
that <s>Mātaṅga</s> maiden who had been seen at the audience hall.

children.text: atha sā praviśya vitatena tejasā dadatīva dikṣu śaradinducandrikām /
children.translated_text: Then she, entering, with her radiance spreading wide, as if bestowing the moonlight of an autumn moon upon the quarters,
with a voice surpassing the sounds of the flute and the <s>vallakī</s> (lute), began to speak:

children.text: he rohiṇīramaṇa sarvakalāniketa tārāpate rajaninātha sudhānidhāna /
children.translated_text: 'O lord of <s>Rohiṇī</s>, abode of all arts, lord of the stars, sovereign of the night, repository of nectar —
O Moon! Remember yourself, whose affections are bound to the qualities and essence of <s>Kādambarī</s>, whose body has been offered!'

children.text: māṃ ca viddhi śaśaketana śriyaṃ sāham asya jananī durātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Know me as <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), O moon-crested one; I am the mother of this wicked one.

children.text: pūrvaceṣṭitam avaitv ato bhavān ity amuṃ tava samīpam ānayam //
children.translated_text: Let the lord know his former deeds — thus have I brought him to your presence.'

children.text: ayam api guruśāsanāṃ vilaṅghya smaraparatantramanāḥ prayātukāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: He too, having transgressed his guru's command, his mind enslaved by <s>Smara</s> (love), wishing to depart,
was then observed by his father with unfailing yogic sight, who suspected his waywardness.

children.text: tasyājñayaivam anubhāvayituṃ vipākam āsannam eva guruśāsanalaṅghanasya /
children.translated_text: By his [father's] command alone, in order to make him experience the imminent fruit of transgressing the guru's command,

children.text: atrāvatīrya vipine janasaṅgabhītyā mātaṅgabhaṅgim avalambya tathā sthitāsmi //
children.translated_text: having descended here, in this forest, out of fear of human contact, assuming the form of an elephant, I have remained thus.

children.text: gacchantam enaṃ viniyamya pāśais tīvrāṇi duḥkhāny anubhāvayantī /
children.translated_text: Binding him as he went with fetters, making him experience severe sufferings,

children.text: śāpāvasānaṃ yuvayoḥ kratoś ca samāptim āsaṃ ciram īkṣamāṇā //
children.translated_text: I was long watching for the end of the curse for both of you and the completion of the sacrifice.

children.text: muner avabhṛthāvadhiḥ pitur amuṣya siddhaḥ kratuḥ kṛtas tvam api saṃsmṛtasvatanur adya tacchāsanāt /
children.translated_text: The sage's sacrifice, whose limit was the concluding ablution, has been accomplished by his father; and you too, today, by his command, have remembered your own [original] body.
Therefore, both of you, having abandoned these bodies resembling shed impurity, now experience the union with your beloveds in your own [true] forms.
Having said this aloud, as if worshipping the earth with flower-petals scattered from the garland loosened by the haste of her departure,

children.text: dikcakraṃ ca pracalaraśanānūpurotthair ninādair āmantryeva drutam udapatad dyām asau divyakāntiḥ //
children.translated_text: and as if bidding farewell to the circle of directions with the sounds arising from her swaying girdle-bells and anklets, she of divine radiance swiftly flew up to the sky.
Seeing her fly up to the sky, whose moonlight was surpassed by the radiance of her own body,

children.text: suciram ūrdhvaniveśitalocanaḥ kam api vismayam āpa jano 'khilaḥ //
children.translated_text: all the people, their eyes fixed upward for a long time, experienced an indescribable wonder.
Then, in the heart of this King <s>Śūdraka</s>, with the series of virtues like steadfastness cast aside,
<s>Madana</s> (love), having found an opening through the continuous memory of <s>Kādambarī</s>, surged forth.

children.text: na rājalakṣmīṃ bahu manyate sma norvīṃ na kīrtīṃ na sarasvatīṃ ca /
children.translated_text: He no longer valued royal fortune, nor the earth, nor fame, nor <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning);

children.text: sa tadrasakṣība ivālalambe kādambarīm eva nitāntam antaḥ //
children.translated_text: as if intoxicated by that passion, he clung solely to <s>Kādambarī</s> in his heart.

children.text: parāṅmukhaḥ sparśaraseṣv ajasraṃ nādatta karṇau madhure 'pi sa dhvanau /
children.translated_text: Averse to the pleasures of touch, ceaselessly not lending his ears even to sweet sounds,
his gaze settled on nothing visible — gradually he lost the function of all his senses.

children.text: na guror upadeśam agrahīd bubudhe vastu tato na mūḍhadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: He did not heed the instruction of his guru; his mind confused, he understood nothing thereafter;

children.text: yatate sma na tasya siddhaye na parispanditum apy apārayat //
children.translated_text: he did not strive for its attainment, nor was he even able to stir.

children.text: bhūtābhibhūta iva mūḍha iva krameṇa niḥsaṃjñatāṃ virahavedanayopanītaḥ /
children.translated_text: As if possessed by spirits, gradually brought to unconsciousness by the pain of separation,

children.text: muktvā manobhavarujaṃ suciraṃ sa rājā prāṇān mumoca sahasaiva vihaṅgamo 'pi //
children.translated_text: that king, having long endured the affliction of love-sickness, suddenly gave up his life — and [so did] the parrot too.

children.text: jīvātmakaṃ cāndramasaṃ ca tejaḥ kṛtāspadaṃ tasya tanau yadāsīt /
children.translated_text: The vital and lunar radiance that had taken abode in his body

children.text: tad eva saṃkrānamathānyadehe citrā hi viśvaprakṛter vikārāḥ //
children.translated_text: now passed into another body — for wondrous indeed are the transformations of universal nature.
Meanwhile, for the daughter of <s>Citraratha</s>, who daily worshipped the body of her beloved,

children.text: tathaiva kālaḥ sumahānagacchad āchodatīre tapasi sthitāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: a very long time passed in the same manner, as she remained in austerity on the shore of the <s>Acchodā</s> lake.

children.text: atha madhusamaye vijṛmbhite sā madanamahotsavavāsare sarāgam /
children.translated_text: Then, when the spring season had blossomed, on the festival day of the great celebration of <s>Madana</s> (love),
she adorned her husband's body excessively with sandalwood, fragrant essences, garlands, and flowers.

children.text: taṃ vīkṣya tāpasadṛśāpi tadā jagāma kāmasya gocaram asau madhujṛmbhitasya /
children.translated_text: Seeing him then, though she resembled an ascetic, she fell within the range of <s>Kāma</s>, aroused by spring;

children.text: ekākinī sapad dikṣu nidhāya cakṣuḥ kāntaṃ svapantam iva nirbharamāliliṅga //
children.translated_text: alone, casting her eyes in all directions, she tightly embraced her beloved who seemed to sleep.

children.text: candrāpīḍaṃ sā ca jagrāha gāḍhaṃ kaṇṭhasthāne jīvitaṃ ca prapede /
children.translated_text: She grasped <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> firmly around the neck, and life returned to him;

children.text: tenāpūrvāṃ sā samullāsalakṣmīm induspṛṣṭā sindhuveleva bheje //
children.translated_text: thereby she attained an unprecedented splendor of joy, like the tide of the ocean touched by the moon.

children.text: śilāśayyāṃ tyaktvā tadanu cirasuptotthita iva kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā jṛmbhālasavadanam unmīlya nayane /
children.translated_text: Then, leaving the stone bed, like one awakened from a long sleep, pausing for a moment, yawning with drowsy face, opening his eyes,

children.text: tataś candrāpīḍaḥ prahatamurajadhvānapaṭunā svareṇa svenaiva smitamadhuram āha priyatamām //
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> spoke to his beloved with a smile, sweetly, in a voice as accomplished as the sound of a beaten drum.

children.text: tvagamṛtaprabhave 'psarasāṃ kule sutanu janma samarthitavaty asi /
children.translated_text: 'O slender one, you have justified your birth in the family of <s>Apsarases</s>, whose origin is nectar of the skin;

children.text: yad amunā parirambhalavena te sapadi jīvitam āpad ayaṃ janaḥ //
children.translated_text: for by this mere touch of your embrace, this person has instantly regained life.'

children.text: mām anvabībhavad imām iyatīm avasthāṃ śāpaḥ kalaṅka iva kāntiharo dvitīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A curse befell me, like a second blemish that steals beauty, bringing about this present state;

children.text: tvadviprayogakṛta eva babhūva tāpas tanvaṅgi śūdrakatanor api mṛtyave me //
children.translated_text: the torment caused by separation from you, O slender-limbed one, became the cause of death for me even in the body of <s>Śūdraka</s>.'

children.text: saṃrakṣitā tanur iyaṃ tu tava priyeti śāpaḥ kṛśodari virāmam avāpa pāpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But [I endured] because this body of yours, my dear, was to be protected' — [thus] the wicked curse came to an end.

children.text: adyaprabhṛty akhilam eva hi candralokaṃ śādhi svapādakṛtamudram imaṃ ca lokam //
children.translated_text: 'From this day forward, rule over the entire lunar realm, and this world marked by your feet.'
'Behold <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, your friend's beloved, his divine life restored by his father's austerities,

children.text: manmaṇḍalād avatarantam akhaṇḍakāntim āpāṇḍugaṇḍam avalokaya puṇḍarīkam //
children.translated_text: his lotus-hand placed in <s>Kapiñjala's</s> grasp, descending from my lunar realm with undiminished beauty, his cheeks free from pallor.'

children.text: kautūhalāt saha mayaiva gatendulokam ālokayiṣyasi kadācana pattralekhām /
children.translated_text: 'One day you will visit the lunar world with me and see <s>Pattralekhā</s> too, out of curiosity;

children.text: kāpi priye sahacarī mama sā tatastyā mā te 'dya bhūt tadanavāptikṛto viṣādaḥ //
children.translated_text: she is a companion of mine there, O dear one — therefore let there be no sadness for you today at not having obtained her.'

children.text: śrutveti tasya giram utsukatāṃ gatāsau romāñcakañcukamakṛtrimam udvahantī /
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, <s>Kādambarī</s>, overcome with eagerness, wearing a natural garment of goosebumps,
fell at the feet of her lord, the beauty of her eyes sprinkled with teardrops of bliss.

children.text: utthāya tvaritopasṛtya ca mahāśvetāṃ pariṣvajya sā pratyakṣīkṛtapuṇḍarīkapadavīṃ kṛtvā ca labdhotsavām /
children.translated_text: Rising quickly, approaching and embracing <s>Mahāśvetā</s>, and having shown her the path [to reunion] with <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> now made visible, making her joyful,

children.text: diṣṭyā vardhayituṃ nyayuṅkta rabhasenāhūya keyūrakaṃ tārāpīḍatapovane parijanaṃ pitror gṛhe cāparam //
children.translated_text: she eagerly summoned <s>Keyūraka</s> and dispatched him to convey congratulations, along with attendants at <s>Tārāpīḍa's</s> hermitage and others at her parents' home.
<s>Tārāpīḍa</s>, though emaciated, came there swiftly, accompanied by his joyful harem, attendants, and minister-retinue;

children.text: tasmin kāle sakhisahacaraḥ puṇḍarīko 'pi nākāt kiñcillajjāvanatavadano vallabhāṃ svām upetaḥ //
children.translated_text: at that time, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> too, accompanied by his friend, descended from heaven, his face slightly bowed with bashfulness, and approached his beloved.

children.text: candrāpīḍaḥ svām api jānann atha mūrtiṃ tārāpīḍaṃ putravad eva praṇanāma /
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, even knowing his own [true] identity, bowed to <s>Tārāpīḍa</s> as if to a father;

children.text: tadvat taṃ ca praśrayaśīlaḥ śukanāsaṃ dattānando 'vandata sarvāś ca janitrīḥ //
children.translated_text: likewise, being of respectful nature, he bowed to <s>Śukanāsa</s>, bestowing joy, and to all his mothers.

children.text: māyā dhātur iyaṃ bhaved bhagavataḥ kiṃ śvetaketor idaṃ sāmarthyaṃ tapasām athendumahasām atrendrajālāyitam /
children.translated_text: 'Could this be the illusion of the blessed Creator? Or is this the power of <s>Śvetaketu's</s> austerities? Or here, is it the magic of the lunar radiance?

children.text: vaiśampāyana ity avedi yad asāv eko 'pi tadbandhubhir yac cāsau sa tu puṇḍarīka iti te tasmin bhave saṃsthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: That <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, as he was known by his kinsmen, is indeed that <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> — they remained [confused] about his identity in that existence.'

children.text: sa puṇḍarīko munir apy apaśyad ātmānam antaḥ śukanāsaputram /
children.translated_text: That sage <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> too recognized himself within as the son of <s>Śukanāsa</s>;

children.text: praṇamya bhūmau pitaraṃ krameṇa manoramādyā jananīr vavande //
children.translated_text: prostrating on the ground before his father, he then bowed in order to his mothers — <s>Manoramā</s> and the others.
Then <s>Vilāsavatī</s> and <s>Manoramā</s>, streams of milk flowing from their breasts,
experienced the great festival of embracing their son's body — the fulfillment of all their desires.

children.text: tārāpīḍas tu pādānatam anavarataprasrutānandabāṣpaś candrāpīḍaṃ bhujābhyāṃ katham api sahasotthāpya kaṇṭhe gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>, with tears of joy streaming ceaselessly, having somehow quickly raised <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> who had fallen at his feet, grasping him by the neck with both arms,

children.text: śāpenātrāvatīrṇo yadi tad api bhavān uttamo lokapālaḥ prakhyāpyeti pratīpaṃ praṇatatanur asāv asya pādau vavande //
children.translated_text: said: 'Even if you have descended here by a curse, you are still the supreme guardian of the world' — proclaiming this with humility, he himself bowed at his feet.

children.text: tasmai nivedya nṛpacakram anicchate 'pi yatnāt kramopanatayā saha rājalakṣmyā /
children.translated_text: Entrusting to him the royal sovereignty, together with the royal fortune that had gradually come [under his care], even though [<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>] was unwilling,

children.text: nojjhāñcakāra cirasaṃcitam āśramaṃ sat tatprārthito 'pi mahiṣīsahitaś caturtham //
children.translated_text: [<s>Tārāpīḍa</s>] did not abandon his long-accumulated noble hermitage, even when entreated by him, but [retired] with his chief queen to the fourth [stage of life].

children.text: ājagmus tatra valgatturagakhurapuṭoddhūtadhūlīkaḍāraiś cūḍāpratyuptabhāsvanmaṇiruciruciraiḥ śobhamānāḥ śirobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: There came the lords of kings, resplendent with heads adorned by the radiance of lustrous gems set in their diadems,

dust raised by the prancing hooves of their horses, their lotus-eyes fully blooming with the eagerness to see <s>Candrāpīḍa</s>, the moon [incarnate], their magnificent gifts prepared with guileless enthusiasm.
Together with <s>Citraratha</s> and his wine, and <s>Haṃsa</s> together with <s>Gaurī</s>,

children.text: sārdhaṃ citrarathas tato madirayā haṃsaś ca gauryā saha draṣṭuṃ nṛttamayīm iva vyavasitām ājagmatur medinīm //
children.translated_text: they came to behold the earth that seemed to have been turned into a [stage for] dance, amidst the clapping of the <s>Gandharva</s> women's hands, whose troop was swelling with the exuberance of joy at gains exceeding their expectations.

children.text: tābhyām etya nirasya tāpasatanucchāyāṃ duhitroḥ kṛte bhāsvatkautukamaṅgale navavadhūveṣe manohāriṇi /
children.translated_text: By those two [parents], coming and having the ascetic appearance cast off from their daughters, a bright auspicious wedding-ceremony for the new brides was arranged in enchanting wedding attire;

children.text: nirvṛtte ca samantrahomasubhagārambhe vivāhotsave tatrānyonyasamāgamapramuditāḥ sarve mudaṃ lebhire //
children.translated_text: and when the wedding festival, graced with mantras, oblations, and auspicious beginnings, was completed, all present, delighted by each other's reunion, attained joy.

children.text: iti vitatavilāsaḥ puṇḍarīkeṇa sākaṃ divi bhuvi ca vicitrodyānalīlāvihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, with expansive sport together with <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, with delightful garden-pleasures and diversions in heaven and on earth,
with ever-growing joy at the attainment of desired fruits, the Moon in the form of <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> enjoyed prosperity.
Thus ends the eighth <s>sarga</s> (canto) of the <s>Kādambarīkathāsāra</s>, composed by <s>Abhinanda</s>, son of the illustrious <s>Bhaṭṭa Jayanta</s>, the emperor among all the learned.
